S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode makes individual object versions write-once-read-many (WORM) for the specified retention period: NO user or AWS process — including the account root user — can delete or shorten the retention on a Compliance-mode locked object once set; the mode cannot be changed or removed during retention. DataSync copies on a schedule (minimum 15-minute batches) rather than automatically on each write. Versioning + lifecycle policies preserve versions but don't prevent deletion (versions can still be permanently deleted). MFA Delete requires MFA for delete-marker creation but the root user with MFA device can still delete — Compliance mode provides stronger guarantees.
tags: Implementing policies for data access, lifecycle, and protection
Storage options and characteristics (for example, durability, replication)

stem: A solutions architect is selecting the correct AWS Glue component for four data engineering tasks. Match each task to the MOST appropriate Glue component. Each component is used once.

answers.A: AWS Glue Crawler
answers.B: AWS Glue ETL Job
answers.C: AWS Glue Data Catalog
answers.D: AWS Glue DataBrew

subquestions.prompt: A data engineering team needs a serverless metadata repository that stores table schemas, partition information, and data locations, making data in S3 and RDS discoverable by Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift Spectrum, and Amazon EMR — all via a single unified metadata API.

The same team needs to automatically scan new S3 prefixes daily, detect schemas for CSV, JSON, Parquet, and Avro formats, identify partitions, and register or update table definitions in the central metadata store — without writing any schema-inference code.

A daily pipeline must join clickstream data from S3 with customer records from Amazon RDS, apply custom aggregation logic in Apache Spark, deduplicate records, and write the result as Parquet files to a new S3 prefix on a managed Spark cluster.

A data analyst (non-engineer) needs to interactively profile 200 GB of messy CSV files, visualise data quality statistics, fix date format inconsistencies, remove duplicate rows, and standardise column values using a visual point-and-click interface — without writing Python or Spark code.

explanation: The Glue Data Catalog is the centralised, persistent, serverless metadata repository: it stores table definitions (column names, types, partitions, locations) and is natively integrated with Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR as their default metastore. Glue Crawlers are the auto-discovery agents: they connect to data stores, infer schemas (including nested types and partitions), and populate or update Catalog table definitions on a schedule. Glue ETL Jobs are managed Apache Spark environments for complex data transformations: they support Python shell and Spark scripts, DynamicFrame APIs, and job bookmarks for incremental processing. AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool: analysts profile datasets (null counts, distributions, patterns), apply 250+ built-in transformations through a point-and-click interface, and publish recipes without writing code.
tags: Data transformation services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Glue)

stem: A company must choose between Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS for two workloads. Workload A is a new cloud-native microservices application whose small team has no Kubernetes expertise and wants AWS-native integration with minimal operational complexity. Workload B is an ML team's existing Kubeflow-based MLOps pipeline that relies on Kubernetes Operators, custom resource definitions (CRDs), Helm chart deployments, and GPU scheduling. Which TWO statements correctly guide the platform decision? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type is the lower-overhead choice for Workload A — it uses AWS-native constructs (task definitions, services, clusters) without a Kubernetes control plane, and integrates natively with ALB, IAM, CloudWatch, and Service Discovery
answers.B: Amazon ECS supports Kubernetes Operators and custom resource definitions through the AWS ECS CRD Bridge — allowing Kubeflow pipelines to be run on ECS without modifications
answers.C: Amazon EKS is the correct platform for Workload B — it runs fully managed Kubernetes and natively supports Kubeflow Operators, Helm charts, custom CRDs, GPU node scheduling (with EC2 launch type using p4d/g5 instances), and the full Kubernetes ecosystem
answers.D: Amazon EKS fully manages the Kubernetes control plane AND worker node scaling, patching, and OS updates — customers have no operational responsibility for any Kubernetes infrastructure
answers.E: Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS have equivalent operational complexity; the primary selection criterion should be whether the team prefers JSON task definitions or YAML pod specs

explanation: Amazon ECS is a native AWS container orchestration service using task definitions, services, and clusters — integrating deeply with ALB (for HTTP routing), IAM (for task roles), CloudWatch, and App Mesh. Teams without Kubernetes experience can deploy and operate ECS with minimal learning curve. Amazon EKS is managed Kubernetes: AWS manages the control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler) but customers manage worker nodes (EC2 or Fargate) and Kubernetes resources. EKS fully supports the standard Kubernetes ecosystem: CRDs, Operators, Helm, Kubeflow, GPU scheduling (via device plugins on EC2 nodes), and any CNCF tooling — making it the only viable choice for Kubeflow-based MLOps. ECS has no concept of Kubernetes Operators or CRDs. EKS customers are responsible for worker node patching and upgrades even though the control plane is managed — using managed node groups reduces but does not eliminate node operational tasks.
tags: The orchestration of containers (for example, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)

stem: A solutions architect is recommending Amazon RDS and Aurora capabilities for three different availability and scaling requirements. Match each requirement to the MOST appropriate database feature. Each feature is used once.

answers.A: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment
answers.B: Amazon RDS Read Replicas
answers.C: Amazon Aurora Global Database

subquestions.prompt: A web application's read workload has grown to 20× the write workload. The team needs to distribute SELECT queries across multiple database endpoints to reduce load on the primary instance — accepting slightly stale reads due to asynchronous replication lag.

A business-critical application requires automatic database failover within 60–120 seconds when the primary AZ becomes unavailable, with synchronous replication guaranteeing zero data loss at failover and no changes to the application's connection string.

A global banking application requires an Aurora database that serves low-latency reads from three secondary Regions, achieves near-zero RPO using storage-level replication with typical lag under 1 second, and can complete a managed cross-Region failover in under 1 minute.

explanation: RDS Read Replicas use asynchronous replication to scale read-heavy workloads: up to 15 replicas for Aurora (5 for other engines) each provide their own connection endpoint; replicas may have slight replication lag, making them unsuitable for strongly consistent reads. RDS Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication to a standby in a second AZ; AWS automatically fails over to the standby (DNS endpoint unchanged) within 60–120 seconds without data loss — the standby does NOT serve read traffic during normal operation. Aurora Global Database uses physical storage-level replication to propagate changes to up to 5 secondary Regions with sub-second lag (typically <1s); secondary clusters serve local reads; managed cross-Region failover completes in under 1 minute with near-zero RPO — designed for globally distributed applications and multi-Region DR.
tags: Disaster recovery (DR) strategies (for example, backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active failover, recovery point objective [RPO], recovery time objective [RTO])

stem: A premium video streaming service distributes licensed content through Amazon CloudFront. Two requirements must be enforced at the CDN edge: (1) only authenticated subscribers with a time-limited token may access individual video files — unauthenticated requests must receive 403 Forbidden, and (2) users in countries where the content is not licensed must be blocked at CloudFront before the request reaches the origin. Which TWO CloudFront features should the architect configure? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: CloudFront Signed URLs — each video URL is signed with an RSA private key, embedding a policy with an expiration time and (optionally) allowed IP range; CloudFront validates the signature at the edge and returns 403 for invalid or expired requests
answers.B: AWS WAF rate limiting rules attached to the CloudFront distribution — limits the number of requests per IP address per minute, preventing unauthenticated bulk access to video files
answers.C: CloudFront Geo Restriction (geographic restrictions) — blocks content delivery to specified countries based on the viewer's IP geolocation determined at the CloudFront edge, before the request reaches the origin
answers.D: AWS Shield Advanced applied to the CloudFront distribution — automatically detects and mitigates volumetric DDoS attacks targeting the video delivery infrastructure from restricted countries
answers.E: Lambda@Edge on the Origin Request trigger to call an authentication microservice for every cache miss, validating the subscriber's session token before fetching content from the S3 origin

explanation: CloudFront Signed URLs embed a cryptographic signature (using an RSA key pair) and an access policy (expiration, allowed IPs, allowed paths) directly in the URL: CloudFront edge servers verify the signature and policy before serving any content, returning 403 for invalid, expired, or tampered URLs. This is the canonical solution for per-subscriber, time-limited content authorization. CloudFront Geo Restriction uses MaxMind IP geolocation to determine the viewer's country at the edge and blocks or allows delivery based on a configurable allowlist or blocklist — with no origin round-trip for blocked countries. WAF rate limiting prevents scraping but does not authenticate individual subscribers or provide time-limited access. Shield Advanced protects against volumetric DDoS, not unauthorized subscriber access. Lambda@Edge for authentication works but adds latency and cost compared to the built-in Signed URL mechanism.
tags: Implementing policies for data access, lifecycle, and protection
Securing external network connections to and from the AWS Cloud (for example, VPN, AWS Direct Connect)

stem: A solutions architect is assigning AWS Organizations policy types to four governance scenarios. Match each scenario to the MOST appropriate Organizations policy type. Each type is used once.

answers.A: Service Control Policies (SCPs)
answers.B: Tag Policies
answers.C: Backup Policies
answers.D: AI Services Opt-out Policies

subquestions.prompt: A data residency policy requires that no EC2 instance can be launched in the ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) Region across any member account. Even if an account administrator grants RunInstances permission in IAM, the launch must be denied.

A FinOps team wants to enforce that all new resources in every member account carry the tags 'Environment' (values: prod, staging, dev) and 'CostCenter' (values: a valid 4-digit code) — flagging non-compliant resources for remediation.

A compliance officer wants daily backup plans (30-day retention) and monthly backup plans (7-year retention) automatically deployed via AWS Backup to all EC2 EBS volumes and RDS instances in all member accounts without any per-account action.

A privacy counsel must ensure that Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Rekognition, Amazon Textract, and Amazon Translate never use the organisation's content to improve AWS's AI/ML models — across all current and future member accounts.

explanation: SCPs are guardrails that restrict what actions principals in member accounts can perform — a Deny SCP on ec2:RunInstances with a region condition prevents launches in the restricted Region regardless of IAM permissions. Tag Policies define tag key naming conventions and allowed values; AWS enforces them across member accounts and reports non-compliant resources through the Organizations console. Backup Policies deploy AWS Backup backup plans to member accounts via Organizations, automatically applying backup schedules and retention rules without per-account configuration. AI Services Opt-out Policies allow an organization to opt all member accounts out of having their content used by AWS for AI model improvement — a single policy covers all listed AI services for current and future accounts.
tags: Designing a security strategy for multiple AWS accounts (for example, AWS Control Tower, service control policies [SCPs])
Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity
Designing appropriate backup and retention policies (for example, snapshot frequency)

stem: An e-commerce company needs two capabilities: (1) a product-catalog search backend supporting full-text queries with fuzzy matching, relevance scoring, and autocomplete suggestions, and (2) real-time operational dashboards showing error-rate trends, p99 latency, and user-activity patterns from application logs shipped from Amazon EC2 instances. Which TWO Amazon OpenSearch Service capabilities directly address these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: OpenSearch's Lucene-based full-text search engine with custom analyzers, fuzzy matching (Levenshtein edit distance), BM25 relevance scoring, and completion suggester for product-catalog autocomplete
answers.B: OpenSearch Serverless — automatically scales search capacity to zero between product searches, eliminating idle search costs for low-traffic windows
answers.C: OpenSearch Dashboards — provides Kibana-compatible visualizations (line charts, heatmaps, data tables), saved searches, index-pattern discovery, and alerting for real-time operational log analytics dashboards
answers.D: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with OpenSearch as the destination — ships logs from EC2 instances to OpenSearch with automatic index creation, satisfying both search and analytics requirements without additional services
answers.E: OpenSearch Machine Learning Commons — automatically classifies product queries using built-in NLP models for relevance re-ranking without requiring Comprehend or SageMaker

explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service's core full-text search engine (based on Lucene) supports custom analyzers, fuzzy queries, BM25 relevance, autocomplete (completion suggester), and phrase-matching — purpose-built for product catalog search. OpenSearch Dashboards (the managed Kibana equivalent) provides interactive visualizations, index-pattern management, Discover (log browsing), Visualize (charts), and Dashboard (multi-panel views) — the standard AWS tool for real-time log analytics. These two capabilities address both requirements within a single managed service. OpenSearch Serverless does not scale to zero; it has a minimum capacity OCU cost even when idle. Kinesis Firehose can deliver logs to OpenSearch (requirement 2) but does not address product-catalog search (requirement 1). ML Commons is an advanced feature not central to the stated requirements.
tags: Data analytics and visualization services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon QuickSuite)

stem: A solutions architect is configuring Amazon Route 53 routing policies for four use cases. Match each use case to the MOST appropriate Route 53 routing policy. Each policy is used once.

answers.A: Weighted routing
answers.B: Geolocation routing
answers.C: Geoproximity routing (Route 53 Traffic Flow)
answers.D: Multivalue Answer routing

subquestions.prompt: A team is performing a canary release of a new API version. Initially 5% of traffic should reach the new version; after validation the weight shifts to 50%, then 100% — all using the same DNS name with no changes to client configuration.

A legal firm's SaaS application must route EU users exclusively to servers in eu-west-1 and North American users to us-east-1, regardless of measured network latency, to comply with GDPR data residency requirements.

A startup runs servers in us-east-1 and eu-central-1. After adding a new location in us-west-2, the team wants to gradually expand the geographic catchment area of us-west-2 by adjusting a bias value, without hard-coding geographic boundaries. Route 53 Traffic Flow is already in use.

A small application runs on 6 web servers (no load balancer). The team wants Route 53 to return up to 8 healthy server IP addresses per DNS query so clients can select from multiple IPs — providing simple client-side load distribution with health-check filtering.

explanation: Weighted routing assigns a numeric weight to each record and distributes queries proportionally — ideal for canary or blue/green deployments where a precise traffic split percentage is required. Geolocation routing maps user locations (continent, country, subdivision) to specific records regardless of latency — ensuring data residency compliance by routing EU users to EU endpoints. Geoproximity routing (available through Route 53 Traffic Flow) routes traffic based on the geographic location of resources and users, with an adjustable bias value that expands or shrinks the geographic area a resource attracts — providing fine-grained geographic load shifting. Multivalue Answer routing returns up to 8 healthy records per query (filtered by health checks) in random order, allowing clients to use any returned IP — providing basic load distribution without requiring a load balancer.
tags: Network services with appropriate use cases (for example, DNS)
Disaster recovery (DR) strategies (for example, backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active failover, recovery point objective [RPO], recovery time objective [RTO])

stem: A company stores 10 TB of structured sales data in Amazon RDS MySQL where complex analytical queries take 30+ minutes. An analytics team also has 500 TB of semi-structured historical data in Amazon S3 (Parquet format) that they need to join with the structured data without running ETL jobs. The team runs unpredictable ad-hoc queries with no consistent workload pattern. Which TWO Amazon Redshift capabilities should the architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Amazon Redshift RA3 nodes — separate storage and compute, automatically archiving cold data to S3 with AQUA acceleration for sub-second query performance on the 10 TB structured dataset
answers.B: Amazon Redshift Serverless — automatically provisions and scales Redshift compute for ad-hoc query workloads without managing clusters; billed per Redshift Processing Unit (RPU) second consumed
answers.C: Amazon Redshift Spectrum — allows Redshift queries to scan data directly from S3 (Parquet, ORC, CSV) at query time, enabling JOINs between Redshift tables and S3-based external tables without ETL ingestion
answers.D: Amazon Redshift cross-Region snapshot copy — replicates the Redshift data warehouse to eu-west-1 for disaster recovery, improving query performance through data locality for European analysts
answers.E: Amazon Redshift Concurrency Scaling — automatically adds transient clusters to serve concurrent read queries when the main cluster queue is full, improving performance for spikes in simultaneous users

explanation: Amazon Redshift Serverless eliminates cluster management for ad-hoc workloads: it automatically provisions capacity when queries arrive and scales to zero between queries — paying only per RPU-second consumed rather than for continuously running cluster nodes. This is the ideal choice when query patterns are unpredictable. Amazon Redshift Spectrum extends Redshift SQL queries to data stored in S3: by defining external tables in the Glue Data Catalog, analysts can JOIN Redshift tables with S3 Parquet files in a single query, with the query engine pushing down predicates to S3 — no ETL required to ingest the 500 TB of historical data. RA3 nodes are best for steady, predictable workloads requiring cluster management. Cross-Region snapshots are for DR, not query performance. Concurrency Scaling handles simultaneous user bursts on a managed cluster, not unpredictable ad-hoc workloads.
tags: Database types and services (for example, serverless, relational compared with non-relational, in-memory)
Data analytics and visualization services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon QuickSuite)

stem: A solutions architect is implementing AWS Config compliance capabilities. Match each compliance requirement to the MOST appropriate AWS Config capability. Each capability is used once.

answers.A: AWS Config managed rules
answers.B: AWS Config custom Lambda rules
answers.C: AWS Config conformance packs
answers.D: AWS Config proactive evaluation

subquestions.prompt: A security team needs out-of-the-box compliance checks for common misconfigurations: S3 buckets with public ACLs, EC2 instances without VPC, and EBS volumes that are unencrypted — using AWS-provided rule definitions without writing any evaluation code.

A governance team must enforce a company-specific policy: EC2 instances must have an 'Approved' tag with a value from a list stored in AWS SSM Parameter Store. No AWS managed rule supports this dynamic lookup logic.

A compliance officer needs to deploy a complete PCI DSS compliance assessment (containing 28 Config rules mapped to PCI DSS controls) across all 25 accounts in the AWS Organisation using a single policy document and track aggregate compliance status.

A DevSecOps team wants AWS Config to evaluate whether a new CloudFormation resource change will violate security policies BEFORE CloudFormation deploys the change — preventing non-compliant resources from being created in the first place.

explanation: AWS Config managed rules are pre-built compliance checks written by AWS (e.g., s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, encrypted-volumes, ec2-instance-in-vpc) that evaluate resources against AWS best practices and compliance frameworks — no code required. Custom Lambda rules evaluate resources against organisation-specific logic written in Lambda functions; the Lambda receives configuration item data and returns compliant/non-compliant — required for dynamic policy lookups. Conformance packs bundle multiple Config rules and remediation actions into a YAML template deployable across an Organisation via StackSets, with aggregate compliance reporting across accounts. Proactive evaluation integrates AWS Config with CloudFormation hooks: rules are evaluated against the planned resource configuration before deployment, blocking non-compliant changes.
tags: Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity

stem: A large enterprise uses AWS Transit Gateway to connect 200 VPCs across multiple accounts and on-premises networks. The security team requires ALL east-west traffic between VPCs to pass through a centralised intrusion detection and prevention system (IDPS) transparently — without making changes to individual VPC routing or application configuration. Which TWO services form the correct centralised inspection architecture? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: AWS Transit Gateway with a dedicated inspection VPC attachment and Transit Gateway route tables configured so all inter-VPC traffic is directed to the inspection VPC's appliance subnet before continuing to its destination
answers.B: AWS Network Firewall deployed in the inspection VPC — provides stateful Layer 3-7 packet inspection, Suricata-compatible intrusion detection and prevention rules, and domain-based traffic filtering for all transiting east-west flows
answers.C: AWS WAF attached directly to the Transit Gateway as a transit policy to inspect Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic between VPCs without requiring a dedicated inspection VPC
answers.D: Amazon GuardDuty with VPC Flow Log analysis to detect suspicious east-west traffic patterns and automatically update security group deny rules to block suspicious flows between VPCs
answers.E: Inter-VPC security groups referencing each other across all 200 VPCs to restrict which VPCs can communicate with which other VPCs, replacing the need for inline IDPS inspection

explanation: The centralised inspection architecture for Transit Gateway works by configuring TGW route tables to 'hairpin' all east-west VPC-to-VPC traffic through an inspection VPC: pre-inspection routes send all traffic to the inspection VPC attachment; post-inspection routes return traffic to the destination VPC. This creates transparent inline inspection without modifying individual VPCs. AWS Network Firewall is deployed in the inspection VPC: it provides stateful and stateless packet inspection at Layers 3–7, Suricata-compatible IDS/IPS rule groups, and domain/IP filtering — satisfying the IDPS requirement. AWS WAF operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and is attached to ALBs, CloudFront, or API Gateway — not to Transit Gateway. GuardDuty provides threat intelligence but is not an inline IDPS and security group modifications are too slow for real-time traffic blocking. Security groups control connectivity but do not inspect packet content.
tags: Designing VPC architectures with security components (for example, security groups, route tables, network ACLs, NAT gateways)
Network routing, topology, and peering (for example, AWS Transit Gateway, VPC peering)

stem: A solutions architect is selecting Amazon FSx file system options for three workloads with distinct requirements. Match each workload to the MOST appropriate FSx file system. Each option is used once.

answers.A: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
answers.B: Amazon FSx for Lustre
answers.C: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

subquestions.prompt: A company running Windows-based EC2 instances needs a shared SMB file share with full Active Directory integration, DFS Namespace support, Windows shadow copies, and NTFS ACL compatibility for a Microsoft SQL Server log shipping target.

A genomics HPC cluster running on AWS uses Slurm to schedule parallel compute jobs. The shared storage must deliver millions of IOPS with sub-millisecond latency, be POSIX-compatible, support striped layouts, and link directly to an S3 data repository for importing input files and exporting results.

An enterprise is migrating a NetApp storage environment to AWS and needs a managed file system that simultaneously supports NFS, SMB, and iSCSI protocols, provides native ONTAP features (SnapMirror replication, FlexClone, deduplication), and can tier cold data automatically to Amazon S3.

explanation: FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed Windows-native file system: it provides SMB protocol, Active Directory authentication, DFS namespaces, shadow copies (point-in-time snapshots visible via Windows), and full NTFS ACLs — the correct choice for Windows workloads and SQL Server integration. FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, high-performance parallel file system optimised for HPC: it delivers sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s throughput; it is POSIX-compatible and directly links to S3 buckets as a persistent repository, enabling automatic import/export of data between Lustre and S3 — ideal for genomics and ML workloads. FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a fully managed ONTAP service offering native multi-protocol access (NFS, SMB, iSCSI), all ONTAP data management capabilities (SnapMirror, FlexClone, deduplication, compression), and automatic S3 tiering — designed for enterprise storage migrations.
tags: Storage options and characteristics (for example, durability, replication)
Hybrid storage options (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A company grants developers the ability to create IAM roles for their Lambda functions. The security team has two concerns: (1) developers must not be able to create Lambda execution roles with permissions exceeding their own IAM permissions — preventing privilege escalation through role creation, and (2) team-created roles that grant unintended cross-account access to S3 buckets or other resources must be automatically detected. Which TWO IAM capabilities address both concerns? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: IAM Permission Boundaries attached to developer IAM roles — the boundary defines the MAXIMUM permissions any role the developer creates can have; even if the developer attaches AdministratorAccess to a Lambda role, effective permissions are the intersection of the attached policies and the boundary
answers.B: AWS Organizations SCPs denying iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy in developer accounts — prevents all role creation, ensuring developers cannot create any execution roles
answers.C: IAM Access Analyzer with the account or Organization as the zone of trust — continuously analyzes IAM role policies, S3 bucket policies, and KMS key policies to automatically generate findings for any resource or role accessible from outside the trust boundary
answers.D: AWS Config managed rule (iam-no-inline-policy) with automatic remediation that detaches inline IAM policies from Lambda execution roles — ensuring no custom permissions are attached
answers.E: Amazon CloudTrail with a CloudWatch Metric Filter that alerts when iam:CreateRole is called — providing a notification to the security team within 5 minutes so they can manually review the newly created role

explanation: IAM Permission Boundaries are the correct mechanism for delegated administration: a developer's IAM role has a permission boundary that limits what maximum permissions any role they create can have. Even if the developer explicitly attaches AdministratorAccess to a new Lambda role, the effective permissions are intersected with the boundary — the Lambda role cannot exceed the developer's own ceiling. IAM Access Analyzer continuously monitors resource-based policies using automated reasoning to identify any principal from outside the zone of trust (account or Organisation) that can access resources — generating findings for cross-account role trust policies, S3 bucket policies, and KMS key grants with external access. Denying all role creation breaks the developer workflow. Config's iam-no-inline-policy detaches inline policies but doesn't prevent overly permissive managed policy attachments. CloudTrail alerting is reactive and manual, not automated detection of cross-account access.
tags: Designing a role-based access control strategy (for example, AWS STS, role switching, cross-account access)
Designing a flexible authorization model that includes IAM users, groups, roles, and policies

stem: A solutions architect is selecting the right AWS integration service for five different business requirements. Match each requirement to the most appropriate AWS service.

answers.A: Amazon AppFlow
answers.B: AWS AppSync
answers.C: Amazon EventBridge
answers.D: AWS Step Functions
answers.E: Amazon SQS

subquestions.prompt: Bidirectional data synchronization between Salesforce CRM and Amazon S3 on a scheduled or event-triggered basis, without writing custom integration code.
A mobile application requires real-time collaborative features where multiple clients subscribe to data changes and receive updates within milliseconds using GraphQL subscriptions.
Route events from 40 different SaaS partners and AWS services to specific Lambda targets based on content-based filtering rules, with schema discovery and registry.
An order fulfillment workflow requires coordinating six Lambda functions with conditional branching, parallel execution, retry logic, and human approval steps, with complete execution history.
Decouple a high-throughput inventory service from downstream processing consumers. Messages must be retained for up to 14 days and processed exactly once using deduplication IDs.

explanation: AppFlow handles SaaS-to-AWS data integration (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk) without custom code. AppSync provides managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions. EventBridge is the event bus for SaaS integrations with content-based routing and schema registry. Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows with branching, parallelism, and human tasks. SQS (FIFO) decouples producers/consumers with exactly-once processing and 14-day retention.

stem: A financial services company operates a mission-critical Aurora MySQL database. The RPO must be under 1 second and the RTO under 1 minute for a regional failure. The application also requires read scaling across three AWS regions for global users. Which TWO features of Aurora should be configured to meet these requirements?

answers.A: Enable Aurora Global Database with managed planned failover, promoting a secondary region within 1 minute.
answers.B: Configure Aurora Multi-AZ with six-way replication across three Availability Zones in the primary region.
answers.C: Enable Aurora write forwarding on Global Database secondary clusters so regional readers can also process writes.
answers.D: Create cross-region Aurora Read Replicas in each target region using binary log replication.
answers.E: Enable Aurora Serverless v2 to automatically scale read capacity based on global traffic patterns.

explanation: Aurora Global Database replicates with typical lag under 1 second (physical replication at the storage layer, not binlog) and managed failover completes in under 1 minute, meeting both RPO and RTO requirements. Write forwarding (option C) allows applications connected to secondary clusters in other regions to send writes, which are forwarded to the primary — enabling true multi-region read/write without application-level routing logic. Option B (Multi-AZ) protects against AZ failure only, not regional failure. Option D (cross-region read replicas via binlog) has much higher replication lag — typically seconds to minutes — failing the RPO. Option E (Serverless v2) scales capacity but doesn't address cross-region DR or RPO/RTO.

stem: A network architect must implement private connectivity from a VPC to multiple AWS services without traversing the internet. Match each AWS service or connectivity scenario to the correct VPC endpoint type.

answers.A: Gateway endpoint
answers.B: Interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink)
answers.C: Gateway Load Balancer endpoint
answers.D: VPC Peering
answers.E: Transit Gateway

subquestions.prompt: Provide private access to Amazon S3 from within a VPC at no additional cost by adding a route table entry. The endpoint policy can restrict access to specific S3 buckets.
Provide private access to Amazon DynamoDB from within a VPC at no additional cost. Traffic stays on the AWS network and does not require a NAT gateway.
Allow EC2 instances in a private subnet to communicate with AWS Systems Manager APIs without internet access. The endpoint appears as an ENI with a private IP in the VPC.
Allow applications to publish records to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams from a private subnet. This creates a private DNS name resolvable within the VPC.
Route traffic through a third-party virtual appliance (IDS/IPS) deployed in a security-focused VPC, allowing the appliance vendor to expose their service to customer VPCs.

explanation: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB — they are free, use route table entries, and don't require ENIs. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) create ENIs with private IPs and support most AWS services (SSM, Kinesis, Secrets Manager, etc.) as well as third-party services — they incur hourly and data processing charges. Gateway Load Balancer endpoints enable transparent insertion of third-party virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS) into the traffic path using the GWLB endpoint service model.

stem: A data platform team needs to trigger downstream processing whenever objects with the prefix 'raw/' and suffix '.parquet' are uploaded to an S3 bucket. They require the ability to fan out to three different Lambda functions, an SQS queue, and a Kinesis stream simultaneously. They also need retry logic with a dead-letter queue for failed event deliveries. Which TWO approaches correctly fulfill all requirements?

answers.A: Enable S3 Event Notifications directly targeting all five destinations simultaneously with prefix/suffix filtering.
answers.B: Enable Amazon S3 to send events to Amazon EventBridge, then create five separate EventBridge rules with prefix/suffix pattern matching targeting each destination, with a DLQ configured on each rule target.
answers.C: Configure S3 Event Notifications to send to a single SNS topic, then subscribe Lambda functions, SQS, and Kinesis as SNS subscribers to fan out.
answers.D: Use S3 Batch Operations to trigger processing of uploaded Parquet files across multiple targets.
answers.E: Enable S3 Event Notifications to a single SQS FIFO queue and use Lambda event source mapping with parallelization factor to fan out to multiple destinations.

explanation: S3 Event Notifications (option A) cannot target multiple destinations simultaneously — each notification configuration points to a single target (Lambda, SQS, or SNS). Option B uses EventBridge (which S3 natively integrates with) — EventBridge supports prefix/suffix filtering via object key patterns, fan-out via multiple rules, and DLQ per target. Option C (SNS fan-out) is a valid classic pattern: S3 notifies SNS, which fans out to Lambda, SQS, HTTP, and Kinesis (via Firehose subscription). Lambda/SQS can be directly subscribed; Kinesis requires a Lambda subscriber. Both B and C correctly satisfy multi-target fan-out. Option D (Batch Operations) processes existing objects, not new uploads. Option E (FIFO SQS) doesn't natively fan out — consumers compete for messages.

stem: A solutions architect is advising on EC2 placement strategies for four workloads. Match each workload description to the most appropriate EC2 placement group type or strategy.

answers.A: Cluster placement group
answers.B: Partition placement group
answers.C: Spread placement group
answers.D: No placement group (default)
answers.E: Dedicated Hosts

subquestions.prompt: A tightly coupled HPC simulation requires all 64 compute nodes to achieve network latency under 25 microseconds and maximize throughput between nodes. Availability is secondary to performance.
A Hadoop cluster with 200 nodes requires fault isolation so that a rack power failure affects at most 25 nodes. The HDFS replication factor of 3 must not have all replicas on the same physical rack.

Seven critical application servers run an active-active database cluster. Each instance must be on distinct underlying hardware so that the failure of any single server does not affect more than one cluster node.
A Microsoft SQL Server workload requires BYOL licensing compliance. The license is tied to specific physical socket counts and the team needs visibility into which physical host each VM runs on.
A fleet of 500 stateless web tier instances processes independent HTTP requests. Fault isolation between specific instances is not required, and the team prioritizes simplicity and cost.

explanation: Cluster placement groups pack instances on same/nearby hardware for ultra-low latency — ideal for HPC with MPI. Partition placement groups divide instances across logical partitions (each partition = separate rack/power/network), letting Hadoop-aware apps control replica placement. Spread placement groups place each instance on distinct hardware (max 7 per AZ) for maximum isolation of critical instances. Dedicated Hosts provide per-socket/per-core visibility for BYOL licensing. Default placement is appropriate for stateless workloads where isolation overhead adds no value.

stem: A media company delivers video thumbnails globally via CloudFront. The origin is an Application Load Balancer in us-east-1. During peak events, the origin receives 50,000 requests per second due to cache misses from 25 regional edge caches simultaneously. The team needs to collapse these into the minimum origin requests while maintaining cache efficiency. Which TWO CloudFront features should be enabled?

answers.A: Enable CloudFront Origin Shield in the AWS Region closest to the origin (us-east-1) as an additional caching layer between regional edge caches and the origin.
answers.B: Configure a minimum TTL of 0 seconds and maximum TTL of 31536000 seconds, allowing the origin Cache-Control headers to govern caching behavior.
answers.C: Enable CloudFront request collapsing (also called request coalescing) by ensuring the cache policy does not include unnecessary headers, cookies, or query strings in the cache key.
answers.D: Configure a Lambda@Edge function at the origin request event to deduplicate identical requests before forwarding to the ALB.
answers.E: Enable CloudFront field-level encryption to reduce the payload size of cache misses sent to the origin.

explanation: Origin Shield adds a centralized caching layer between all 25+ regional edge caches and the origin. Instead of each POP sending cache miss requests directly to the origin, they funnel through Origin Shield — which serves from its own cache. This dramatically reduces origin load during peak events. Request collapsing (coalescing) is a built-in CloudFront behavior: when multiple requests for the same object arrive simultaneously at an edge location while a cache miss is in flight, CloudFront holds the subsequent requests and serves them all from the single origin response. To maximize coalescing, the cache key must be as narrow as possible — unnecessary headers/cookies/query strings create spurious cache key variations that prevent collapsing. Option B describes TTL configuration but does not reduce origin requests. Option D (Lambda@Edge deduplication) is complex, adds latency, incurs per-request costs, and is not the correct mechanism. Option E (field-level encryption) is for data protection, not request reduction.

stem: A cloud financial management team is implementing a cost optimization program. Match each optimization objective to the most appropriate AWS service or feature.

answers.A: AWS Compute Optimizer
answers.B: AWS Cost Explorer
answers.C: AWS Budgets
answers.D: AWS Trusted Advisor
answers.E: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR)

subquestions.prompt: Identify over-provisioned EC2 instances by analyzing 14 days of CloudWatch metrics and recommend the optimal instance type, including cross-family recommendations (e.g., m5.xlarge → r6g.large).
Visualize Reserved Instance utilization and coverage over the past 12 months, identify underutilized RIs, and generate purchase recommendations based on historical On-Demand usage.
Send an alert via email when forecasted monthly spend for the production account exceeds $50,000, and automatically invoke an SNS action when actual spend reaches 80% of budget.
Automatically check for idle load balancers, underutilized EBS volumes, and unassociated Elastic IP addresses across the account and surface them in a consolidated dashboard.
Generate hourly line-item billing data including resource tags, usage type groups, and reservation/savings plan amortization for ingestion into a custom Athena + QuickSight analytics pipeline.

explanation: Compute Optimizer uses ML on CloudWatch metrics to recommend right-sized instance types including cross-family moves (x86→ARM Graviton). Cost Explorer has built-in RI utilization/coverage reports and purchase recommendation engine. Budgets supports forecasted and actual thresholds with SNS/email actions. Trusted Advisor provides automated best-practice checks including idle resources and cost checks (checks vary by support tier). CUR is the most granular billing data source — hourly line items with resource-level tags, suitable for custom BI pipelines via Athena.

stem: A processing pipeline uses SQS standard queues with Lambda consumers. Messages represent video transcoding jobs that take 8–12 minutes to process. The team observes that messages are being processed multiple times, and the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible metric is consistently at 1000 (the maximum concurrent Lambda invocations). Which TWO configuration changes will resolve the duplicate processing while maintaining throughput?

answers.A: Increase the SQS visibility timeout to 15 minutes to ensure the message remains hidden from other consumers while being processed.
answers.B: Enable SQS long polling with a wait time of 20 seconds to reduce the frequency of empty ReceiveMessage responses.
answers.C: Switch to an SQS FIFO queue to guarantee exactly-once processing with message deduplication IDs.
answers.D: Increase the Lambda reserved concurrency limit and use Lambda's maximum batch window of 300 seconds to batch messages.
answers.E: Request a service quota increase for Lambda concurrent executions and configure the SQS event source mapping to use a maximum concurrency setting that matches the quota.

explanation: Duplicate processing occurs because the visibility timeout (default 30 seconds) expires before the 8–12 minute job completes, making the message visible again and triggering another consumer. Setting visibility timeout to 15 minutes (the maximum) ensures the message stays hidden during processing. The concurrent execution cap at 1000 causes a backlog — when Lambda throttles, the SQS event source mapping retries retrieval, which can cause messages whose visibility timeout expired to be re-delivered. Requesting a quota increase and configuring maximum concurrency on the event source mapping (a newer feature that limits per-source concurrency without affecting other Lambda functions) both address throughput and reduce the backlog-driven redelivery. Option B (long polling) reduces empty responses but does not address duplicate processing. Option C (FIFO) has a 3,000 msg/sec throughput cap and exactly-once requires deduplication IDs — helpful for exact-once but doesn't fix the timeout issue and limits scale. Option D (batch window) is for aggregating messages, not preventing duplicates.

stem: A data engineering team is building a real-time analytics platform. Match each data streaming requirement to the correct Amazon Kinesis service.

answers.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
answers.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
answers.C: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
answers.D: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
answers.E: Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka)

subquestions.prompt: Multiple independent analytics applications must consume the same clickstream data at their own pace, replaying up to 7 days of historical records. Each consumer maintains its own checkpoint in the shard.
IoT sensor readings must be buffered and delivered to Amazon S3 in Parquet format with GZIP compression, partitioned by arrival time, without writing any consumer code.

A fraud detection system must join a stream of financial transactions against a reference table, compute tumbling window aggregates every 60 seconds, and emit alerts when anomaly scores exceed a threshold.

Security cameras at 2,000 retail locations must stream live H.264 video to AWS for computer vision analysis using Amazon Rekognition Video. The service must handle stream ingestion, storage, and playback.
An existing on-premises Apache Kafka application must be migrated to AWS with minimal code changes. The team requires Kafka-native APIs, topic-based routing, and consumer group semantics.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams supports multiple independent consumers (Enhanced Fan-Out or standard), custom retention up to 365 days, and shard-level checkpointing. Kinesis Data Firehose is the zero-code delivery service to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch with built-in format conversion (JSON→Parquet) and compression. Managed Apache Flink (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics for Flink) provides stateful stream processing with SQL/Java/Python, windowing functions, and stream joins. Kinesis Video Streams is purpose-built for video ingestion, storage, and playback with Rekognition Video integration. MSK is the managed Kafka service — use when Kafka API compatibility is required.

stem: A company requires 20 Gbps of dedicated bandwidth between its on-premises data center and AWS. The connectivity must be redundant against a single port failure at the Direct Connect location. The company wants to maximize bandwidth while using the fewest number of physical connections. Which TWO configurations meet these requirements?

answers.A: Provision a single 10 Gbps Dedicated Connection and enable jumbo frames to increase effective throughput to 20 Gbps.
answers.B: Create a Link Aggregation Group (LAG) with two 10 Gbps Dedicated Connections to the same Direct Connect location, achieving 20 Gbps aggregate bandwidth with port-level redundancy.
answers.C: Provision two 10 Gbps Dedicated Connections at different Direct Connect locations and configure BGP equal-cost multipath (ECMP) routing to aggregate the bandwidth across both connections.
answers.D: Order a single 100 Gbps Dedicated Connection and configure a minimum links setting of 1 in the LAG to provide automatic failover.
answers.E: Create a LAG with four 10 Gbps Dedicated Connections, achieving 40 Gbps total capacity with the LAG minimum links set to 2 so the LAG fails if more than two ports fail.

explanation: A Link Aggregation Group (LAG) bundles multiple Dedicated Connections from the same Direct Connect location into a single managed connection. Two 10 Gbps connections in a LAG provide 20 Gbps aggregate and survive a single port failure if minimum-links is set to 1. Option C uses ECMP across two connections at different locations — BGP with equal-cost paths aggregates bandwidth and provides location-level redundancy (stronger than port-level). Option A is incorrect: jumbo frames reduce overhead but do not increase the 10 Gbps physical port limit. Option D (single 100 Gbps connection) provides no port redundancy — it is a single point of failure. Option E achieves 40 Gbps with redundancy but exceeds the 20 Gbps requirement with more connections than necessary.

stem: A security operations team is selecting the right AWS security service for five distinct threat detection and investigation scenarios. Match each scenario to the most appropriate AWS service.

answers.A: Amazon GuardDuty
answers.B: Amazon Macie
answers.C: Amazon Inspector
answers.D: Amazon Detective
answers.E: AWS Security Hub

subquestions.prompt: An EC2 instance is communicating with known cryptocurrency mining pools. The security team needs an agentless service that continuously analyzes VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and DNS logs to detect this threat.

Automatically discover and classify S3 buckets that contain Social Security numbers, credit card data, and passport numbers, then alert the security team to buckets with overly permissive ACLs containing PII.
Continuously scan all EC2 instances and container images in ECR for CVEs listed in the NVD database and provide a risk score based on network reachability and package exploitability.

After GuardDuty raises a finding for credential compromise, investigate the full scope of activity by an IAM role over the past 12 months using interactive graph visualizations of CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty data.

Aggregate security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and third-party SIEM tools into a single dashboard, normalize them to a standard format, and track remediation status across 50 AWS accounts.

explanation: GuardDuty is the agentless threat detection service analyzing VPC Flow Logs/CloudTrail/DNS. Macie uses ML to discover and protect sensitive data in S3. Inspector scans EC2/ECR for CVEs and network exposures. Detective provides forensic investigation with visual analytics on historical log data — it ingests GuardDuty, CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and builds behavioral baselines. Security Hub aggregates findings across services and accounts, normalizes to ASFF format, and provides compliance dashboards.

stem: A company runs a stateful session processing application on Auto Scaling EC2 instances behind an ALB. When scale-in occurs, in-flight sessions must complete before instance termination. The warm-up period for new instances is 4 minutes (application initialization). Which TWO configurations ensure sessions complete on termination and new instances are ready before receiving traffic?

answers.A: Create a lifecycle hook for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING state with a heartbeat timeout of 3600 seconds, and use a Lambda function triggered by EventBridge to drain sessions and call CompleteLifecycleAction.
answers.B: Enable Connection Draining (Deregistration Delay) on the ALB target group with a 300-second timeout so the ALB stops routing new requests to instances being terminated and waits for in-flight requests.
answers.C: Set the Auto Scaling group's default cooldown period to 240 seconds so scale-in actions wait 4 minutes before terminating instances.
answers.D: Configure the ALB to use slow start mode with a 240-second duration so new instances receive a gradually increasing share of traffic during their 4-minute initialization.
answers.E: Set instance scale-in protection on all instances and use a custom script to remove protection only after sessions drain, triggered by an SNS notification from the lifecycle hook.

explanation: Lifecycle hooks (option A) pause instance termination at the EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING state, allowing a Lambda function to detect the termination, drain active sessions, and then call CompleteLifecycleAction to proceed. The heartbeat timeout can be extended up to 2 hours. Option D (ALB slow start mode) gradually ramps traffic to new instances over a configurable duration (30–900 seconds), preventing new instances from being overwhelmed before their 4-minute initialization completes. Option B (Connection Draining) handles ALB-level session draining for registering/deregistering targets but it works with target deregistration — not the lifecycle hook directly. The question specifies sessions that must complete on termination, which requires the lifecycle hook to trigger the drain action first. Option C (cooldown) prevents subsequent scale-in events but does not drain sessions from the terminating instance. Option E (instance scale-in protection + SNS) is overly complex and protection removal via scripts is error-prone.

stem: A solutions architect must select the right serverless or managed compute service for five different application requirements. Match each requirement to the most appropriate AWS compute service.

answers.A: AWS Lambda
answers.B: AWS Fargate
answers.C: AWS App Runner
answers.D: Amazon ECS Anywhere
answers.E: AWS Batch

subquestions.prompt: Process S3 object creation events to extract metadata and write to DynamoDB. Each invocation processes a single file in under 30 seconds with no idle-time charges.
Run a containerized microservice with 4 vCPU and 30 GB RAM requirements. The service has unpredictable traffic and the team must not manage EC2 instances or patching.

Deploy a containerized web application from a GitHub repository with automatic builds, deployments, and scaling. The team has no container orchestration expertise and wants the simplest path from code to URL.
Run ECS task definitions on on-premises servers that cannot be migrated to AWS due to data sovereignty requirements, while managing the tasks from the AWS console.
Execute 10,000 genomics analysis jobs that each run for 2–6 hours on spot instances, with automatic job queuing, dependency management, and retry logic for spot interruptions.

explanation: Lambda is best for event-driven, short-duration (≤15 min) functions with no idle cost. Fargate removes EC2 management for containers with flexible vCPU/memory configurations. App Runner is the simplest path for containerized web apps — source-to-URL with no ECS/Fargate knowledge required. ECS Anywhere extends ECS control plane to on-premises/edge servers for data sovereignty scenarios. AWS Batch manages job queues, compute environments, and dependencies for large-scale batch workloads, optimizing spot instance usage with automated retry.

stem: A software vendor needs to access resources in 500 different customer AWS accounts to deliver a monitoring service. Each customer grants the vendor access to their account. The vendor's security team is concerned about the confused deputy problem. Which TWO IAM mechanisms correctly address both the cross-account access requirement and the confused deputy vulnerability?

answers.A: Require each customer to create an IAM role with a trust policy that allows the vendor's AWS account to assume it, and include an sts:ExternalId condition in the trust policy with a unique, customer-specific external ID.
answers.B: Require each customer to create an IAM user with access keys and share those keys with the vendor's monitoring service via AWS Secrets Manager.
answers.C: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share the customer's IAM roles directly with the vendor's account, eliminating the need for AssumeRole calls.
answers.D: Require each customer to add the vendor's IAM role ARN to the aws:PrincipalArn condition of a resource-based policy on each monitored resource.
answers.E: Configure STS session policies when calling AssumeRole to scope the vendor's permissions to only the resources required for monitoring, reducing the blast radius if credentials are compromised.

explanation: The confused deputy problem occurs when a vendor's service is tricked into using its elevated privileges to access a customer's account without the customer's authorization. The mitigation is the ExternalId condition (option A): each customer generates a unique external ID, embeds it in their trust policy, and shares it with the vendor privately. When the vendor's service assumes the role, it must provide the correct external ID — preventing an attacker who knows the vendor's account ID from having the vendor access their account. Option E (session policies) further limits the permissions in each AssumeRole session to exactly what's needed, reducing blast radius. Option B (IAM user access keys) is an anti-pattern for cross-account access and violates least privilege/credential rotation best practices. Option C is incorrect — RAM shares resources (not IAM roles) across accounts. Option D (resource-based policies) works for some services but requires updating policies on every monitored resource — impractical at 500 customers.

stem: A migration team must move data from various sources to AWS. Match each data migration scenario to the correct AWS service.

answers.A: AWS DataSync
answers.B: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
answers.C: AWS Snowball Edge
answers.D: AWS Transfer Family
answers.E: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)

subquestions.prompt: Migrate 500 TB of files from an on-premises NFS server to Amazon EFS. The migration must be incremental (sync changed files nightly) and preserve POSIX metadata and timestamps.

Migrate a 2 TB Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with schema conversion. The source database must remain online during migration, with minimal downtime cutover using CDC (Change Data Capture).
Transfer 8 PB of seismic survey data from an oil exploration site with limited (10 Mbps) WAN connectivity. At 10 Mbps, the transfer would take over 2 years over the network.
Provide an SFTP endpoint so that 200 external trading partners can upload financial files directly to S3 without modifying their existing SFTP client configurations.
Lift-and-shift 300 VMware virtual machines to EC2. The service must replicate the source servers continuously, allow non-disruptive testing, and cut over with a final delta sync.

explanation: DataSync is purpose-built for incremental file system migrations (NFS/SMB/HDFS/S3/EFS) with metadata preservation and scheduling. DMS migrates databases with schema conversion (via SCT) and CDC for zero-downtime cutover. Snowball Edge handles petabyte-scale migrations where WAN bandwidth makes online transfer impractical. Transfer Family (SFTP/FTPS/FTP) provides managed file transfer endpoints backed by S3 or EFS. Application Migration Service (MGN) replaces SMS for lift-and-shift VM migrations, using continuous block replication with non-disruptive test cutover.

stem: A team is conducting a Well-Architected Review of a three-tier application. The review identifies that a single slow downstream service call causes cascading failures across all 500 web tier instances within 2 minutes. Which TWO architectural changes directly prevent the cascading failure pattern?

answers.A: Implement a circuit breaker pattern using AWS App Mesh with a timeout policy and outlier detection, automatically ejecting unhealthy upstream endpoints from the load balancing pool.
answers.B: Add CloudWatch alarms on the downstream service's error rate and trigger an Auto Scaling scale-out event for the web tier when errors exceed a threshold.
answers.C: Deploy the downstream service call behind an SQS queue with a visibility timeout equal to the downstream service's SLA, decoupling the web tier from the downstream service's latency.
answers.D: Enable multi-AZ deployment for the downstream service's RDS database to improve its recovery time.
answers.E: Implement bulkhead isolation using separate thread pools or Lambda reserved concurrency limits for the downstream service call, preventing it from consuming all available connections from the web tier.

explanation: Cascading failures occur when a slow dependency holds connections/threads, exhausting the calling service's resource pool. The circuit breaker pattern (option A) — implemented via App Mesh outlier detection or application-level libraries — detects failure and stops sending requests to the unhealthy endpoint, allowing fast-fail rather than timeout-induced connection exhaustion. Bulkhead isolation (option E) limits the blast radius: by constraining the slow service call to a dedicated thread pool or Lambda concurrency allocation, the failure cannot consume resources needed for other operations. Option B (scale-out) adds capacity but does not prevent connection exhaustion — more instances hitting the slow service scales the problem. Option C (SQS decoupling) is valid for asynchronous workloads but fundamentally changes the architecture — it cannot be applied to synchronous web request handling without redesign. Option D (Multi-AZ) improves database availability but doesn't address connection exhaustion in the calling service.

stem: A compliance officer requires different key management solutions for five distinct security requirements. Match each requirement to the correct AWS key and secrets management service.

answers.A: AWS KMS (Customer Managed Key)
answers.B: AWS CloudHSM
answers.C: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
answers.D: AWS Secrets Manager
answers.E: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString)

subquestions.prompt: Encrypt S3 objects using a key that the company exclusively controls. The key policy must prevent AWS employees from accessing plaintext data, and key usage must be logged to CloudTrail.

Generate RSA 4096-bit keys for code signing within a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security module. The company must have exclusive control over the HSM partition and the master keys must never leave the HSM.
Provision a TLS certificate for an ALB and API Gateway. The certificate must auto-renew before expiration and must be free of charge. The private key must never be exportable.
Store an RDS master password and rotate it automatically every 30 days. Lambda functions and ECS tasks must be able to retrieve the current password at runtime without application code changes.
Store non-secret environment-specific configuration strings and a handful of encrypted API keys for a Lambda function. Cost is a concern and automatic rotation is not required.

explanation: KMS CMKs provide AWS-managed HSMs with key policies that enforce exclusive customer control and CloudTrail logging. CloudHSM provides dedicated FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs where the customer owns the partition and keys never leave hardware — required for the highest compliance bar. ACM provisions free TLS certificates for AWS services with automatic renewal; private keys are non-exportable and managed by AWS. Secrets Manager stores secrets with built-in rotation via Lambda, versioning, and cross-account access — purpose-built for credentials. Parameter Store SecureString uses KMS for encryption and is cost-effective (free tier for standard parameters) for configuration/non-rotation use cases, though it lacks automatic rotation.

stem: A company with 120 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations needs to enforce that: (1) no account can disable AWS CloudTrail, (2) S3 public access block is enabled in all accounts, and (3) new accounts are automatically provisioned with a standard VPC baseline. Which TWO mechanisms correctly enforce these requirements at scale?

answers.A: Attach an SCP to the root of the organization denying cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and cloudtrail:UpdateTrail for all principals. Apply a separate SCP preventing s3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock from disabling the block.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Config rules using Organization Config Rules (cloudtrail-enabled and s3-account-level-public-access-blocks-periodic) and configure automatic remediation using SSM Automation documents.
answers.C: Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory with customizations (Account Factory for Terraform or CfCT) to automatically apply the VPC baseline CloudFormation template to every new account upon provisioning.
answers.D: Create a CloudWatch Events rule in the management account that detects account creation and triggers a Lambda function to deploy the VPC baseline template via CloudFormation StackSets.
answers.E: Enable AWS Security Hub with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard and suppress findings for the 120 accounts using suppression rules.

explanation: SCPs (option A) are preventive guardrails — they enforce policy by denying API calls regardless of IAM permissions. Denying cloudtrail:StopLogging/DeleteTrail at the org root means no account, including the root user, can disable CloudTrail (unless the management account is exempt). Similarly, denying disabling S3 public access block enforces it organization-wide. Option C (Control Tower Account Factory customizations) automatically provisions VPC baselines to new accounts — this is the correct mechanism for infrastructure baselining of new accounts using CT's lifecycle events. Option B (Config rules) are detective controls, not preventive — they detect non-compliance but cannot block the API call. Option D (CloudWatch Events + Lambda + StackSets) is a valid DIY alternative to Control Tower but is more operationally complex. Option E (Security Hub) is purely detective and reporting.

stem: A data management team is optimizing S3 storage costs. Match each data access pattern or requirement to the most cost-effective S3 storage option.

answers.A: S3 Standard
answers.B: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
answers.C: S3 Standard-IA
answers.D: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
answers.E: S3 Glacier Deep Archive

subquestions.prompt: Machine learning training datasets that are accessed heavily during model training sprints (weekly) and then untouched for months. The access pattern is completely unpredictable and the team cannot predict future access.
Financial audit records that must be retained for 10 years per regulatory requirement. The data is virtually never accessed but must be retrievable within 12 hours if a regulator requests it.

Medical images (X-rays, MRIs) that are accessed frequently in the first 30 days after creation, then once per quarter for follow-up consultations. Retrieval must be in milliseconds and a per-GB retrieval fee is acceptable.
Weekly database backups that are retained for 90 days. The backups are accessed only in disaster recovery scenarios (roughly once per year). A minimum storage duration of 30 days is acceptable.
A web application's static assets (CSS, JS, images) that receive millions of requests per day with sub-millisecond latency requirements and no acceptable retrieval fees.

explanation: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive tiers based on access patterns — ideal for unpredictable workloads. Deep Archive is the lowest-cost option (< $1/TB/month) for data that is almost never accessed with 12-hour retrieval SLA. Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond access like Standard-IA but at Glacier pricing — ideal for quarterly-accessed archival data where retrieval speed matters. Standard-IA suits backups accessed infrequently (with the 30-day minimum storage charge). S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data requiring the lowest latency and no retrieval fees.

stem: A DevOps team is deploying a microservices application on Amazon EKS. Individual pods require different AWS IAM permissions: payment pods need access to a specific KMS key, and analytics pods need access to S3 and Kinesis. The team wants the minimum-privilege principle enforced at the pod level, not at the node level. Which TWO mechanisms correctly implement pod-level IAM in EKS?

answers.A: Configure IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) by annotating each Kubernetes Service Account with the ARN of an IAM role, and configure the IAM role's trust policy to trust the EKS OIDC provider.
answers.B: Assign an IAM instance profile to each node group that grants the superset of all permissions needed by all pods on that node.
answers.C: Use EKS Pod Identity (EKS Pod Identity Agent) to associate IAM roles with Kubernetes Service Accounts via EKS API, eliminating the need to manage OIDC trust policy configurations manually.
answers.D: Inject AWS credentials as Kubernetes Secrets from AWS Secrets Manager using the External Secrets Operator, mounting them as environment variables in each pod.
answers.E: Use Kubernetes Network Policies to restrict which pods can communicate with the AWS metadata endpoint, preventing unauthorized pods from accessing instance profile credentials.

explanation: IRSA (option A) is the original mechanism for pod-level IAM in EKS. Each Kubernetes Service Account is annotated with an IAM role ARN, and the IAM role's trust policy specifies the EKS cluster's OIDC provider and the specific service account namespace/name as conditions. The EKS webhook injects AWS_ROLE_ARN and AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE environment variables into pods, allowing the AWS SDK to assume the correct role. EKS Pod Identity (option C) is the newer, simpler mechanism launched in 2023 that uses an agent DaemonSet instead of OIDC federation. It associates roles with service accounts via EKS API calls rather than requiring manual trust policy edits — simpler to configure and supports role chaining. Option B (node-level instance profile) violates least privilege — all pods inherit the same permissions. Option D (injected secrets) works but rotates credentials statically and doesn't use IAM role assumption. Option E (Network Policies blocking metadata) is a partial security mitigation, not an IAM mechanism.

stem: A social media platform stores user posts in DynamoDB with UserId as the partition key and PostTimestamp as the sort key. The most popular user has 5 million followers and their posts generate 80,000 writes per second to a single partition, far exceeding the 3,000 WCU per partition limit. The team also needs to query posts by geographic region. Which TWO design changes correctly solve these problems?

answers.A: Implement write sharding by appending a random suffix (1-20) to the UserId partition key, distributing writes across 20 partitions, and use scatter-gather reads to aggregate results.
answers.B: Enable DynamoDB Auto Scaling with a target utilization of 50% to automatically provision additional WCUs when the hot partition is detected.
answers.C: Create a Global Secondary Index (GSI) with Region as the partition key and PostTimestamp as the sort key to enable efficient region-based queries without a full table scan.
answers.D: Switch the table to use DynamoDB Streams and process all writes through a Lambda function that distributes items across multiple tables by region.
answers.E: Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) write-through caching to absorb the 80,000 writes per second and reduce the load on the underlying DynamoDB table.

explanation: Write sharding (option A) is the canonical solution for hot partition keys in DynamoDB. By appending a random suffix (e.g., UserId#1 through UserId#20), writes are distributed across 20 partitions at 4,000 WCUs each, easily handling 80,000 WPS. Reads require scatter-gather across all 20 shards, but this is acceptable for read-heavy workloads. A GSI on Region (option C) creates a separate index maintained by DynamoDB, allowing efficient queries like 'all posts from US-WEST' without scanning the full table. Option B (Auto Scaling) adjusts provisioned capacity but cannot split a single hot partition — the partition key determines which physical partition handles the write. Option D (Streams + Lambda + multiple tables) is an anti-pattern that dramatically increases complexity. Option E (DAX) is a read-through/write-through cache but does not reduce write load on the underlying table for unique writes.

stem: A platform engineering team needs to implement various monitoring capabilities using Amazon CloudWatch. Match each monitoring requirement to the correct CloudWatch feature.

answers.A: CloudWatch Logs Insights
answers.B: CloudWatch Contributor Insights
answers.C: CloudWatch Metric Streams
answers.D: CloudWatch Synthetics
answers.E: CloudWatch Application Insights

subquestions.prompt: Run ad-hoc queries against 90 days of application logs to find the top 10 error messages, calculate p99 latency percentiles, and correlate request IDs across multiple log groups.
Identify which IP addresses are responsible for the highest number of 5xx errors on an API Gateway in near real-time, and determine which API paths generate the most throttling.
Forward CloudWatch metrics to a third-party observability platform (Datadog, New Relic) in near real-time via Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, rather than polling the GetMetricData API.
Simulate user journeys (login, checkout, search) against the production application every 5 minutes from multiple AWS regions, and alert when synthetic transactions fail or exceed latency thresholds.

Automatically detect performance anomalies and errors in a .NET application running on EC2 by analyzing CloudWatch Logs patterns and correlating them with infrastructure metrics, without manual alarm configuration.

explanation: Logs Insights provides a query language (similar to SQL) for searching and analyzing CloudWatch Logs, including aggregations, regex, and stats functions. Contributor Insights analyzes structured log data to identify the top-N contributors to metrics (top talkers, heaviest API consumers). Metric Streams enables continuous streaming of CloudWatch metrics to Kinesis Firehose for forwarding to third-party tools — much lower latency than polling. Synthetics (Canaries) runs scripted user flows on a schedule for synthetic monitoring. Application Insights automatically configures monitoring for known application technologies (.NET, SQL Server, Java) and uses ML to detect anomalies.

stem: A database administrator notices that an RDS MySQL instance has high CPU utilization during business hours despite the queries looking simple. The team suspects lock contention but has no visibility into what is causing the waits. Which TWO actions give the team the visibility needed to identify the root cause?

answers.A: Enable RDS Performance Insights to view database load broken down by wait events, SQL statements, users, and hosts — identifying which queries are contributing to CPU/IO wait.
answers.B: Enable Enhanced Monitoring with a 1-second granularity to view OS-level metrics including per-process CPU, memory, and file system I/O, visible via CloudWatch and the RDS console.
answers.C: Set the slow_query_log parameter in the RDS parameter group to 1 and set long_query_time to 0 to capture all queries to the MySQL slow query log, then publish logs to CloudWatch Logs.
answers.D: Create a CloudWatch alarm on the RDS CPUUtilization metric and trigger an Auto Scaling action to scale up to a larger instance class when CPU exceeds 80%.
answers.E: Enable Multi-AZ on the RDS instance so that read traffic can be distributed to the standby replica, reducing CPU load on the primary.

explanation: Performance Insights (option A) provides a dashboard showing database load (average active sessions) broken down by wait events — critical for diagnosing lock contention. The wait event breakdown shows exactly which locks (innodb_lock, io/file, etc.) are contributing to load. Slow query log (option C) with long_query_time=0 captures every query including those causing locks — publishing to CloudWatch Logs enables querying the logs with Logs Insights. Together, these provide real-time wait event visibility and historical query-level analysis. Enhanced Monitoring (option B) provides OS-level metrics but not database-internal wait events or SQL-level visibility. Option D (scale-up alarm) treats the symptom, not the cause. Option E is incorrect: Multi-AZ standby replicas do NOT serve read traffic — that requires a Read Replica.

stem: A data engineering team needs to build data transformation pipelines for four different workloads. Match each workload to the most appropriate AWS data processing service.

answers.A: AWS Glue ETL (Spark-based)
answers.B: AWS Glue DataBrew
answers.C: AWS Lambda
answers.D: Amazon EMR Serverless
answers.E: AWS Step Functions + AWS Glue

subquestions.prompt: Process 50 TB of raw clickstream data daily: join it with a 500 GB product catalog, deduplicate records, convert JSON to Parquet, and partition by date and region for Athena queries.

A data analyst (non-engineer) needs to clean and normalize a 10 GB CSV dataset by removing null rows, standardizing phone number formats, and creating derived columns — using a visual, no-code interface.

Transform each Kinesis Data Stream record in real-time: parse the JSON, enrich it with a lookup from DynamoDB, and forward the result to a Kinesis Firehose delivery stream. Processing must complete within 500ms.

Run a custom PySpark machine learning feature engineering pipeline that requires 500 vCPUs and custom Python libraries. The job runs for 3 hours weekly and the team wants no cluster management overhead.

Orchestrate a multi-step monthly financial reconciliation: extract from Redshift → transform with Glue → validate with Lambda → load to RDS → notify via SNS, with conditional branching based on validation results.

explanation: Glue ETL (Spark) is ideal for large-scale batch transformations (50 TB) with Spark API familiarity. DataBrew provides a visual, no-code interface for data analysts to clean and transform datasets. Lambda handles real-time, millisecond-latency stream transformations with DynamoDB lookups. EMR Serverless runs custom Spark/Hive jobs at scale without cluster provisioning — ideal for ML feature engineering with custom libraries. Step Functions orchestrates multi-service workflows with conditional branching, error handling, and parallel execution across AWS services.

stem: A global application is deployed in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
