stem: A company wants employees working remotely to access private application instances without exposing SSH or RDP to the internet. Authentication must be per-user through the company identity provider rather than shared network credentials. Which TWO design choices BEST satisfy these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Deploy AWS Client VPN and federate authentication with the corporate identity provider.
answers.B: Allow inbound access to the application instances only from the Client VPN address space or a security group associated with VPN-connected resources.
answers.C: Expose the instances through an internet-facing bastion host with a shared key pair.
answers.D: Use a Site-to-Site VPN from each employee laptop.
answers.E: Assign public IP addresses to all instances and restrict by employee home IP ranges.

explanation: AWS Client VPN is the right service for per-user remote access from laptops, including federated authentication. Instance access should then be scoped so only traffic coming from the VPN-connected network can reach the private application instances. A bastion host with shared credentials or public instance exposure weakens the security posture, and Site-to-Site VPN is for network-to-network connectivity rather than individual end users.
tags: Network connection options (for example, AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink)

stem: A solutions architect is fine-tuning Amazon Route 53 policies for a multi-Region design. Match each requirement to the Route 53 routing policy that BEST satisfies it. Each option is used once.

answers.A: Multivalue Answer
answers.B: Geoproximity
answers.C: Weighted
answers.D: Latency-based

subquestions.prompt: The DNS response should return up to eight healthy records so clients can distribute requests across multiple healthy endpoints without a load balancer.
The team wants to bias more traffic toward one Region by using geography-aware traffic flow, even if users are not strictly closest to that Region.
Exactly 5% of requests should be sent to a canary endpoint while 95% continue to the main endpoint.
Users should normally reach the healthy endpoint that has the lowest measured network latency from their DNS resolver location.

explanation: Multivalue answer routing returns multiple healthy records, allowing simple client-side distribution without a load balancer. Geoproximity routing uses geographic bias to shift traffic toward or away from Regions. Weighted routing is for deliberate percentage-based splits such as canaries. Latency-based routing chooses the endpoint with the best measured latency from the resolver location.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A company runs several public endpoints without a load balancer and wants Amazon Route 53 to return only healthy IP addresses to clients while still providing simple DNS-level distribution across multiple healthy records. Which TWO features are REQUIRED? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Multivalue answer routing
answers.B: Route 53 health checks associated with the records
answers.C: Failover routing only
answers.D: AWS Global Accelerator
answers.E: Geolocation routing

explanation: Multivalue answer routing returns multiple healthy records in DNS responses, but the records must be associated with Route 53 health checks so unhealthy endpoints are removed from responses. Failover routing supports active-passive rather than simple distribution across many healthy records, and Global Accelerator is a different global front-door service.
tags: Identifying metrics based on business requirements to deliver a highly available solution

stem: A solutions architect is choosing the right AWS global traffic optimization service for several use cases. Match each requirement to the BEST-FIT service. Each option is used once.

answers.A: Amazon CloudFront
answers.B: AWS Global Accelerator
answers.C: Amazon Route 53
answers.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration

subquestions.prompt: Static or cacheable content should be served from edge locations worldwide to reduce origin load and latency.
A non-cacheable TCP application needs static anycast IP addresses, fast health-based failover, and optimized global path selection.
DNS-level routing should steer users among regional application endpoints according to policies such as latency or failover.
Clients around the world must upload objects more quickly into a single Amazon S3 bucket without building custom edge proxies.

explanation: CloudFront is the edge caching and content-delivery service for cacheable content. Global Accelerator is for global front-door optimization and fast failover of non-cacheable applications with static anycast IPs. Route 53 provides DNS-level routing policies among endpoints. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads and downloads to a single S3 bucket through the AWS edge network.
tags: Edge networking services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator)
Determining strategic needs for content delivery networks (CDNs) and edge caching

stem: A solutions architect is mapping hybrid networking roles to AWS constructs. Match each role to the AWS construct that BEST fits. Each option is used once.

answers.A: Customer Gateway
answers.B: Virtual Private Gateway
answers.C: AWS Transit Gateway
answers.D: AWS Direct Connect Gateway

subquestions.prompt: Represents the on-premises router or firewall in AWS configuration for a Site-to-Site VPN connection.
Acts as the VPC-side attachment target for a Site-to-Site VPN connection or a private virtual interface into a single VPC.
Provides the central routing hub for many VPC attachments and VPNs in a hub-and-spoke network.
Extends one Direct Connect connection so it can reach associated AWS resources across multiple Regions.

explanation: A Customer Gateway is the AWS-side representation of the on-premises router or firewall for VPN. A Virtual Private Gateway is the VPC-side construct for VPN and private VIF connectivity into a single VPC. Transit Gateway is the hub for many VPCs and VPNs. Direct Connect Gateway extends private Direct Connect reachability across multiple Regions.
tags: Creating a network topology for various architectures (for example, global, hybrid, multi-tier)
Network connection options (for example, AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink)

stem: A company wants its data center to connect by IPsec VPN into a centralized multi-account hub so on-premises prefixes can reach many VPCs through one routing domain. Dynamic route exchange is required. Which TWO design choices BEST meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Attach the VPN to an AWS Transit Gateway.
answers.B: Configure BGP between the on-premises device and AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
answers.C: Create individual VPC peering connections from the data center to each application VPC.
answers.D: Use only static routes because Transit Gateway VPN attachments do not support BGP.
answers.E: Replace the VPN with CloudFront.

explanation: A Transit Gateway is the correct centralized routing hub when on-premises prefixes must reach many VPCs through one routing domain. Site-to-Site VPN with BGP provides dynamic route exchange to and from the on-premises environment. VPC peering does not connect an on-premises network, and Transit Gateway VPN attachments do support BGP.
tags: Creating a network topology for various architectures (for example, global, hybrid, multi-tier)

stem: A company must expose a public API with mutual TLS on a custom domain, while the backend services run privately in VPC subnets. The team wants a managed API layer rather than operating internet-facing reverse proxies. Which TWO design choices BEST satisfy these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Use a Regional API Gateway custom domain configured for mutual TLS.
answers.B: Integrate the private backend through API Gateway VPC Link to a private Network Load Balancer.
answers.C: Use a private API Gateway and expect internet clients to resolve it.
answers.D: Put the backend directly on public EC2 instances and terminate mutual TLS there.
answers.E: Replace API Gateway with S3 Transfer Acceleration.

explanation: Regional API Gateway custom domains support mutual TLS for public API clients without requiring the team to operate its own public reverse proxy layer. VPC Link provides managed private connectivity from API Gateway into a private NLB that fronts backend services in the VPC. A private API Gateway is not publicly reachable by internet clients, and exposing backend instances directly breaks the stated design goal.
tags: API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)

stem: A company serves a global software download portal. Installers and documentation are static and heavily cacheable, but a small set of signed entitlement checks remains dynamic. Regional origin data-transfer cost is rising sharply. Which TWO design choices BEST reduce cost while preserving the dynamic checks? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Serve the static files through Amazon CloudFront.
answers.B: Configure cache behaviors so entitlement-check paths bypass caching and are forwarded to the dynamic origin.
answers.C: Replace the dynamic origin with AWS Direct Connect.
answers.D: Use AWS Global Accelerator instead of CloudFront for the static objects.
answers.E: Move all static files behind a NAT gateway.

explanation: CloudFront is the correct service for offloading origin traffic and reducing transfer cost for heavily cacheable global content. Separate cache behaviors let the static objects remain cached while entitlement-check paths are forwarded dynamically to the origin. Global Accelerator is not a cache, and the other options do not address CDN offload for static content.
tags: Determining strategic needs for content delivery networks (CDNs) and edge caching

Configuring appropriate network routes to minimize network transfer costs (for example, Region to Region, Availability Zone to Availability Zone, private to public, AWS Global Accelerator, VPC endpoints)

stem: A solutions architect is choosing the appropriate front door or load-balancing option for several application protocols. Match each requirement to the BEST-FIT AWS service. Each option is used once.

answers.A: API Gateway HTTP API
answers.B: Application Load Balancer
answers.C: Network Load Balancer
answers.D: AWS Global Accelerator

subquestions.prompt: A fully managed HTTP API needs native JWT authorizers and pay-per-request pricing instead of permanently running load balancer capacity.
A containerized web application needs Layer 7 host-based and path-based routing across multiple services.
A custom TCP protocol requires Layer 4 load balancing with source IP preservation.
A multi-Region application needs one global entry point with static anycast IP addresses over regional ALB or NLB endpoints.

explanation: HTTP API in API Gateway is the lowest-cost managed API front door with features such as JWT authorizers and per-request pricing. ALB is the Layer 7 routing service for host and path rules. NLB is the Layer 4 service for TCP and source IP preservation. Global Accelerator adds a global entry point with static anycast IPs across regional endpoints.

stem: An application in three Availability Zones sends large volumes of Amazon S3 traffic and modest amounts of third-party internet traffic from private subnets. Today all private subnets point to one NAT gateway in a single Availability Zone, causing both NAT processing charges and inter-AZ transfer costs. Which TWO changes MOST directly improve cost efficiency while preserving high availability? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Add a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3.
answers.B: Create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each private subnet to the local NAT gateway.
answers.C: Keep the single NAT gateway but increase its size.
answers.D: Replace S3 access with CloudFront uploads only.
answers.E: Move all subnets into one Availability Zone.

explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint removes the largest class of AWS-bound traffic from the NAT gateway entirely, cutting NAT processing charges. NAT gateways in each Availability Zone keep the remaining internet-bound traffic local to its AZ and avoid inter-AZ data transfer while preserving zonal resilience. Changing NAT size does not change the core pricing problem.
tags: Configuring appropriate NAT gateway types for a network (for example, a single shared NAT gateway compared with NAT gateways for each Availability Zone)

Configuring appropriate network routes to minimize network transfer costs (for example, Region to Region, Availability Zone to Availability Zone, private to public, AWS Global Accelerator, VPC endpoints)

stem: A solutions architect must choose the correct AWS service to restrict or expose several application traffic patterns securely. Match each requirement to the BEST-FIT service or feature. Each option is used once.

answers.A: AWS PrivateLink
answers.B: AWS Client VPN
answers.C: AWS Network Firewall
answers.D: AWS WAF

subquestions.prompt: Expose one private service to many consumer VPCs without providing broad network connectivity and while tolerating overlapping CIDR ranges.
Provide individual remote users with secure access to private VPC resources from laptops.
Perform centralized, stateful inspection and filtering of traffic traversing a VPC.
Filter malicious HTTP request patterns such as SQL injection before they hit the application.

explanation: PrivateLink is the secure one-service exposure pattern for many consumer VPCs without broad network adjacency. Client VPN is the per-user remote access service. Network Firewall provides centralized stateful inspection within the network path. WAF filters malicious Layer 7 HTTP requests before they reach the application.
tags: Control ports, protocols, and network traffic on AWS

stem: A solutions architect is choosing DNS and hybrid name-resolution components for a multi-account environment. Match each requirement to the BEST-FIT AWS capability. Each option is used once.

answers.A: Route 53 Resolver rule shared with AWS RAM
answers.B: Route 53 private hosted zone associated with multiple VPCs
answers.C: Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint
answers.D: Route 53 public hosted zone

subquestions.prompt: Multiple application accounts must use the same forwarding rule for selected corporate domains without recreating the rule in every account.
Internal application records should resolve privately in more than one VPC under AWS control.
On-premises DNS servers must forward queries into AWS so they can resolve private records hosted in a VPC.
Internet users must resolve the company public domain to public-facing endpoints.

explanation: Shared Resolver rules distributed with AWS RAM let multiple accounts reuse centralized forwarding logic. A private hosted zone can be associated with multiple VPCs for internal records. Resolver inbound endpoints allow on-premises DNS to forward queries into AWS. Public hosted zones publish records to the public internet DNS hierarchy.
tags: Creating a network topology for various architectures (for example, global, hybrid, multi-tier)
Determining network configurations that can scale to accommodate future needs

stem: A company wants to expose a private service running on Amazon EC2 to many consumer VPCs in other AWS accounts. Consumer VPC CIDR ranges might overlap, and the provider does not want to grant consumers any general access to the rest of the provider VPC. Which TWO design choices BEST meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Place the service behind a Network Load Balancer in the provider VPC.
answers.B: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by that load balancer.
answers.C: Peer every consumer VPC with the provider VPC.
answers.D: Attach every consumer VPC to a shared AWS Transit Gateway.
answers.E: Expose the service through a public Application Load Balancer and restrict source IPs.

explanation: PrivateLink endpoint services are exposed through a Network Load Balancer in the provider VPC. This pattern lets many consumer VPCs connect privately to one service, even with overlapping CIDR ranges, without granting general network access to the provider VPC. Peering, Transit Gateway, and public ALB exposure violate one or more stated requirements.
tags: Creating a network topology for various architectures (for example, global, hybrid, multi-tier)

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations and AWS IAM Identity Center integrated with an external identity provider. Developers belong to an IdP group named AppDev. Members of AppDev need administrator access in every sandbox account, read-only access in every production account, and no long-lived AWS credentials. The company wants the fewest ongoing manual changes as new accounts are added to the appropriate OU. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Create IAM users in each account for the AppDev users, synchronize passwords from the identity provider, and attach AdministratorAccess in sandbox accounts and ReadOnlyAccess in production accounts.
answers.B: Create two permission sets in IAM Identity Center and assign the AppDev group to each individual account manually whenever a new account is created or moved.
answers.C: Create two permission sets in IAM Identity Center, assign the AppDev group to the Sandbox OU for administrator access and to the Production OU for read-only access, and have users federate through IAM Identity Center.
answers.D: Create one administrator permission set in IAM Identity Center for all accounts, and use service control policies in production accounts to block changes to key services.

explanation: IAM Identity Center permission sets with OU-level assignments provide centralized federation, no long-lived credentials, and low ongoing administrative overhead as accounts are added to the correct OU. Using one broad admin permission set and trying to limit it with SCPs is harder to manage and less aligned with least privilege.
tags: Access controls and management across multiple accounts
AWS federated access and identity services (for example, IAM, AWS IAM Identity Center)
Designing a security strategy for multiple AWS accounts (for example, AWS Control Tower, service control policies [SCPs])

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with dozens of member accounts. Security requirements state that no account administrators may stop organization-wide API activity logging or remove their account from the organization. Local administrators must still retain broad permissions to manage workloads in their own accounts. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend to enforce these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Create an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail that applies to all accounts.
answers.B: Apply a service control policy (SCP) at the root or relevant OUs that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, cloudtrail:UpdateTrail, and organizations:LeaveOrganization.
answers.C: Attach a permissions boundary to each administrator role that denies the actions.
answers.D: Use AWS Config managed rules to detect trail changes and automatically recreate the trail.
answers.E: Grant local administrators read-only IAM access so they cannot affect CloudTrail.

explanation: An organization trail centralizes CloudTrail logging across accounts, and an SCP provides preventive control so local administrators cannot disable logging or leave the organization. Permissions boundaries and Config rules are not organization-wide preventive controls for every admin principal.
tags: Access controls and management across multiple accounts
Designing a security strategy for multiple AWS accounts (for example, AWS Control Tower, service control policies [SCPs])

stem: A company runs Amazon ECS tasks on AWS Fargate in private subnets. The tasks pull container images from Amazon ECR, retrieve database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager, and download startup artifacts from Amazon S3. A new security policy prohibits any internet gateway or NAT gateway access from the private subnets. Which TWO changes will allow the tasks to launch successfully while meeting the policy? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Create interface VPC endpoints for Amazon ECR (API and DKR) and AWS Secrets Manager.
answers.B: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and update the private subnet route tables.
answers.C: Move the Fargate tasks to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
answers.D: Replace AWS Secrets Manager with environment variables stored in the task definition.
answers.E: Add an egress-only internet gateway to the VPC.

explanation: Private Fargate tasks need interface endpoints to reach Amazon ECR and AWS Secrets Manager privately. Amazon ECR image layers are stored in Amazon S3, so a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 is also required. Public subnets and internet gateways violate the policy.
tags: Designing VPC architectures with security components (for example, security groups, route tables, network ACLs, NAT gateways)

stem: A company replicates objects from an Amazon S3 bucket in Account A to a bucket in Account B. The source bucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed KMS key in Account A. The destination bucket must also use SSE-KMS with a different customer managed KMS key in Account B. The company wants native S3 replication with the least operational overhead. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Enable versioning on both the source and destination buckets.
answers.B: Configure the replication rule to use S3 default encryption only because S3 replication cannot replicate KMS-encrypted objects.
answers.C: Update the KMS key policies and IAM role permissions so the replication role can decrypt with the source key and encrypt with the destination key.
answers.D: Configure bucket ACLs that grant the destination account FULL_CONTROL on the source bucket.
answers.E: Use the same KMS key alias name in both accounts so Amazon S3 can map the keys automatically during replication.

explanation: Native S3 replication requires versioning on both buckets. When objects are encrypted with customer managed KMS keys, the replication role must have permission to use the source key for decryption and the destination key for encryption. ACLs and key alias name matching do not satisfy these requirements.
tags: Encrypting data at rest (for example, AWS KMS)
Implementing access policies for encryption keys

stem: A regulated company stores audit evidence in Amazon S3. Compliance requires that, once written, records cannot be deleted or modified by any user, including administrators, until a 7-year retention period expires. The company also needs centralized lifecycle management with minimal custom code. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete on the bucket. Use a bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject to all principals.
answers.B: Store the records in an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, configure a 7-year retention period, and use lifecycle rules for storage class transitions.
answers.C: Replicate the records to another account and use a service control policy (SCP) to deny deletion in both accounts.
answers.D: Store the records on Amazon EFS encrypted with AWS KMS, and use AWS Backup vault lock for 7 years.

explanation: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode is designed for write-once-read-many retention that even administrators cannot override before the retention period ends. Versioning and MFA Delete improve protection but do not provide the same compliance-grade immutability guarantee.
tags: Implementing policies for data access, lifecycle, and protection

stem: A media company runs a fleet of Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones. Each instance must read and write the same shared set of millions of small files with POSIX semantics. The data must remain available if instances are replaced, and the storage layer must scale automatically without re-architecting the application. Which storage solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Create an Amazon EFS file system and mount it from all instances.
answers.B: Attach a Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon EBS volume to each instance and synchronize the data with rsync.
answers.C: Use Amazon S3 with the AWS CLI to copy objects locally before processing.
answers.D: Deploy Amazon FSx for Lustre as scratch storage in one Availability Zone and mount it from all instances.

explanation: Amazon EFS provides shared, durable, multi-AZ file storage with POSIX semantics and elastic scaling, which matches the access pattern and availability requirements. Per-instance EBS volumes and S3 copies do not provide shared file semantics, and scratch FSx for Lustre does not match the durability and multi-AZ requirements.
tags: Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)
Storage types with associated characteristics (for example, object, file, block)
Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs

stem: A company runs a self-managed database on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The workload requires 18,000 sustained IOPS and 600 MiB/s of throughput on one volume. The company wants the lowest-cost Amazon EBS option that meets these performance requirements without changing the application. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.A: A Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume provisioned for 18,000 IOPS.
answers.B: A General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume provisioned for 18,000 IOPS and 600 MiB/s throughput.
answers.C: A Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume sized to maximize throughput.
answers.D: A General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume sized to reach 18,000 IOPS.

explanation: gp3 can be provisioned independently for both IOPS and throughput and is generally the lowest-cost EBS SSD option for this level of performance. io2 would meet the requirement but usually at a higher cost, and st1 and gp2 are poor fits for the stated sustained performance target.
tags: Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs
Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)

stem: A web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. New instances require 12 minutes to download reference data and warm caches before they can serve traffic. Sudden traffic spikes can occur in less than 2 minutes. The company needs a design that preserves elasticity while reducing the time to add capacity during spikes. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Configure a warm pool for the Auto Scaling group so pre-initialized instances are available to enter service quickly.
answers.B: Increase the cooldown period on the Auto Scaling group to 12 minutes.
answers.C: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer.
answers.D: Use scheduled scaling to keep maximum capacity running at all times.

explanation: A warm pool keeps pre-initialized instances ready so they can enter service much faster during sudden spikes while still preserving elastic scaling. Cooldowns and load balancer type changes do not solve long initialization time, and permanently running peak capacity would sacrifice cost efficiency.
tags: Scalability capabilities with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, AWS Auto Scaling)
Identifying metrics and conditions to perform scaling actions
Selecting the appropriate compute options and features (for example, EC2 instance types) to meet business requirements

stem: A SaaS application stores tenant configuration data as key-value items. The application serves users from North America, Europe, and Asia. Each Region must support local read and write traffic with single-digit millisecond latency, and data changes must replicate automatically to the other Regions. Which database solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Amazon Aurora Global Database with one writer Region and read-only secondary Regions.
answers.B: Amazon DynamoDB global tables.
answers.C: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with cross-Region read replicas.
answers.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with Global Datastore.

explanation: DynamoDB global tables provide multi-Region active-active writes with low-latency local access and automatic replication. Aurora Global Database and RDS cross-Region replicas are primarily one-writer designs, and ElastiCache is not a system of record for this requirement.
tags: Database types and services (for example, serverless, relational compared with non-relational, in-memory)
Determining an appropriate database type (for example, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)

stem: A microservices application on Amazon ECS connects to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. During deployment events, many new tasks start at once and open thousands of database connections, causing intermittent timeouts even though the database CPU remains low. The application code cannot be changed quickly. Which solution BEST improves performance and scalability?

answers.A: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of Aurora.
answers.B: Configure Amazon RDS Proxy for the Aurora cluster and have the ECS services connect through the proxy.
answers.C: Increase the Aurora backup retention period so failovers are faster.
answers.D: Replace Aurora with Amazon DynamoDB because DynamoDB does not have connection limits.

explanation: RDS Proxy pools and manages database connections so connection storms from scaling events do not overwhelm the Aurora cluster. A cache may help read performance but does not directly solve connection exhaustion, and switching database engines is unnecessary and high risk for the stated problem.
tags: Determining an appropriate database type (for example, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)

stem: A company runs a containerized video transcoding workload overnight. Jobs are queued in batches, can be retried safely, and must finish before 6:00 AM. The current design uses an always-on fleet of On-Demand Amazon EC2 instances that sits idle during the day. The company wants to minimize cost without increasing operational complexity. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Run the workload on AWS Batch with Spot capacity and retry strategies.
answers.B: Move the workload to AWS Lambda with reserved concurrency equal to the current EC2 fleet size.
answers.C: Purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plan for the existing always-on EC2 fleet.
answers.D: Run the workload on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate with no autoscaling.

explanation: AWS Batch is purpose-built for queued batch jobs and can use Spot capacity with retries for significant savings when workloads are interruptible. This approach avoids paying for idle daytime capacity and does not require managing a custom scheduling stack.
tags: AWS purchasing options (for example, Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans)
Determining cost-effective AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate)
Determining the required availability for different classes of workloads (for example, production workloads, non-production workloads)

stem: A company runs a stateless web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Traffic has a steady baseline every day and an unpredictable burst above that baseline during product launches. The company needs to reduce compute cost without affecting application availability during bursts. Which TWO actions will BEST meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Purchase Savings Plans to cover the steady baseline compute usage.
answers.B: Configure the Auto Scaling group with a mixed instances policy that can use Spot Instances for a portion of burst capacity.
answers.C: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer to reduce hourly cost.
answers.D: Use a single large On-Demand instance instead of an Auto Scaling group.
answers.E: Schedule the Auto Scaling group to stop all instances overnight.

explanation: Savings Plans reduce the cost of the predictable baseline, while mixed instances with Spot can lower the cost of elastic burst capacity without removing the ability to scale on demand. The other options either do not address the main cost driver or would reduce resilience and elasticity.
tags: AWS purchasing options (for example, Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans)
Scaling strategies (for example, auto scaling, hibernation)
Determining appropriate scaling methods and strategies for elastic workloads (for example, horizontal compared with vertical, EC2 hibernation)

stem: A product catalog application currently uses a self-managed document database on Amazon EC2. The application performs simple key-based lookups, experiences unpredictable read traffic with long idle periods and sudden promotional bursts, and does not require joins or complex transactions. The company wants the lowest operational overhead and wants to avoid paying for unused capacity while still delivering single-digit millisecond reads. Which database solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode.
answers.B: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ with Provisioned IOPS storage.
answers.C: Amazon Aurora provisioned with reader Auto Scaling.
answers.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis as the primary data store.

explanation: DynamoDB on-demand is well suited for unpredictable key-value workloads because it avoids capacity planning, provides low-latency reads, and removes the operational burden of managing database servers. The relational options are harder to operate and typically cost more when traffic is bursty and mostly idle between spikes.
tags: Database types and services (for example, relational compared with non-relational, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)
Determining cost-effective AWS database services with appropriate use cases (for example, DynamoDB compared with Amazon RDS, serverless)
Determining an appropriate database type (for example, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)

stem: A company runs workloads in private subnets across three Availability Zones. Most outbound traffic is to Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB, but the workloads currently use NAT gateways for all egress. NAT charges are high. The company needs to reduce network cost without reducing availability. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3.
answers.B: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.C: Replace the three NAT gateways with one shared NAT gateway in a single Availability Zone.
answers.D: Route all private subnet traffic through an internet gateway.
answers.E: Replace the NAT gateways with Application Load Balancers.

explanation: Gateway VPC endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB remove that traffic from the NAT path, which lowers data processing charges and preserves highly available private connectivity. Consolidating to one NAT gateway would reduce resilience and can introduce cross-AZ data transfer charges.
tags: Configuring appropriate network routes to minimize network transfer costs (for example, Region to Region, Availability Zone to Availability Zone, private to public, AWS Global Accelerator, VPC endpoints)
Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations

stem: A company runs a globally distributed TCP application that is hosted behind Network Load Balancers in two AWS Regions. Enterprise customers require static IP addresses for allow lists. The company wants users to connect to the closest healthy Region with fast failover if a Regional endpoint becomes unavailable. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing with alias records to the Network Load Balancers.
answers.B: Use AWS Global Accelerator with the Network Load Balancers as endpoints.
answers.C: Put Amazon CloudFront in front of the Network Load Balancers.
answers.D: Use an Application Load Balancer in one Region and configure cross-Region load balancing.

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses, directs users to the nearest healthy endpoint over the AWS global network, and fails over quickly when an endpoint or Region becomes unhealthy. Route 53 does not provide the same fixed IP model or acceleration path for TCP traffic.
tags: Edge networking services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator)
Selecting the appropriate load balancing strategy

stem: A company runs a stateful web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer across two Availability Zones. User session state is stored in memory on each instance. During an Availability Zone failure, many users are forced to sign in again, and the surviving instances become overloaded. The company wants to improve availability with minimal application changes. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Move session state to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
answers.B: Configure the Auto Scaling group to span multiple Availability Zones and scale on load.
answers.C: Enable sticky sessions on the Application Load Balancer and keep session state on each instance.
answers.D: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer.
answers.E: Store sessions on instance store volumes for faster recovery.

explanation: Externalizing session state to Amazon ElastiCache removes a single-instance dependency, and scaling across multiple Availability Zones improves fault tolerance and recovery capacity. Sticky sessions and instance-local storage keep the architecture dependent on individual instances and do not address AZ failure well.
tags: Implementing designs to mitigate single points of failure
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company operates production workloads in one AWS account and a separate security tooling account. Security engineers need emergency administrator access to the production account only during incidents. The company requires engineers to use their existing identities from the security account, that access be temporary, and that MFA be enforced for the elevation path. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Create IAM users in the production account for each engineer, attach AdministratorAccess, and rotate their access keys in AWS Secrets Manager after every incident.
answers.B: Create an administrator IAM role in the production account that trusts a specific role in the security account, require aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent in the trust or permissions policy, and have engineers assume the role by using AWS STS.
answers.C: Attach AdministratorAccess to the engineers' IAM roles in the security account and rely on AWS Organizations to extend those permissions to the production account.
answers.D: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool for the security team and map the users directly to the root user in the production account during incidents.

explanation: A cross-account IAM role assumed through STS provides temporary credentials, avoids long-lived keys in the production account, and can enforce MFA for the privileged access path. IAM permissions do not automatically extend across accounts, and creating IAM users in production increases administrative risk.
tags: Designing a role-based access control strategy (for example, AWS STS, role switching, cross-account access)
AWS federated access and identity services (for example, IAM, AWS IAM Identity Center)
Applying AWS security best practices to IAM users and root users (for example, multi-factor authentication [MFA])

stem: A company exposes a REST API to an application running in an on-premises data center over AWS Direct Connect. The API must remain private, use AWS-managed authentication and throttling features, and never traverse the public internet. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Create a Regional REST API in Amazon API Gateway with a public endpoint and a resource policy that allows only the on-premises public IP addresses.
answers.B: Create a private REST API in Amazon API Gateway and access it through an interface VPC endpoint in the VPC that is connected to the data center through AWS Direct Connect.
answers.C: Place the API behind an internet-facing Application Load Balancer and restrict source IPs to the data center CIDR ranges.
answers.D: Deploy the API on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets and publish it through Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs.

explanation: A private Amazon API Gateway REST API accessed through an interface VPC endpoint keeps traffic on private connectivity while still providing managed API features such as authorization and throttling. Public endpoints restricted by IP still traverse the public internet and do not meet the stated requirement.
tags: Securing external network connections to and from the AWS Cloud (for example, VPN, AWS Direct Connect)

stem: A company serves a public web application through Amazon CloudFront with an internet-facing Application Load Balancer as the origin. Security requirements state that the origin must accept traffic only from CloudFront, and the application must block common SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts at the edge. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Associate AWS WAF with the Amazon CloudFront distribution and use managed or custom rules for SQL injection and cross-site scripting detection.
answers.B: Restrict the Application Load Balancer security group to the AWS-managed CloudFront origin-facing prefix list.
answers.C: Attach AWS Shield Standard to the Application Load Balancer and define SQL injection and cross-site scripting match rules there.
answers.D: Replace Amazon CloudFront with AWS Global Accelerator so only AWS edge locations can reach the Application Load Balancer.
answers.E: Configure an origin access control on the Application Load Balancer so only CloudFront can connect.

explanation: AWS WAF on Amazon CloudFront inspects requests at the edge for layer 7 attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Restricting the Application Load Balancer security group to the CloudFront origin-facing managed prefix list limits direct origin access. Shield does not provide WAF-style application rules, and origin access control is not an ALB feature.
tags: Threat vectors external to AWS (for example, DDoS, SQL injection)
Integrating AWS services to secure applications (for example, AWS Shield, AWS WAF, IAM Identity Center, AWS Secrets Manager)
Control ports, protocols, and network traffic on AWS

stem: A company has Amazon EBS volumes and Amazon RDS databases in multiple AWS accounts. Compliance requires centrally managed backup policies, cross-account backup copies, and protection against deletion of recovery points before retention expires. The company wants the least operational overhead. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use service-specific snapshots in each account and copy them manually to Amazon S3 buckets with versioning enabled.
answers.B: Use AWS Backup with AWS Organizations backup policies, copy backups to a dedicated backup account, and apply AWS Backup Vault Lock to the destination vault.
answers.C: Enable Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots and use AWS CloudTrail to recover deleted RDS snapshots.
answers.D: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager across all accounts and invoke AWS Lambda functions to copy all backups to another Region.

explanation: AWS Backup provides centralized, policy-based backup management across accounts, supports cross-account copy, and works with both Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS. AWS Backup Vault Lock adds immutability protection for recovery points until the retention period expires, which aligns with the compliance requirement with less operational effort than custom automation.
tags: Aligning AWS technologies to meet compliance requirements

stem: A retailer needs to coordinate payment authorization, inventory reservation, shipment creation, and customer notification for each order. Some steps invoke AWS Lambda functions, some invoke Amazon ECS tasks, and high-value orders require a manual approval before shipment. Each step needs built-in retries, state tracking, and an auditable workflow history. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Publish an event to Amazon SNS for each order and let each downstream system implement its own retries and coordination logic.
answers.B: Send order messages to an Amazon SQS queue and have a single worker service execute all steps in sequence.
answers.C: Store each order in Amazon DynamoDB and use DynamoDB Streams to trigger every step independently.
answers.D: Model the workflow in AWS Step Functions and integrate the state machine with AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, and a manual approval step.

explanation: AWS Step Functions is designed for workflow orchestration across multiple services with retries, branching, human approval integrations, and execution history. SNS, SQS, and DynamoDB Streams can help decouple components but do not provide the same built-in end-to-end orchestration and auditability.
tags: Workflow orchestration (for example, AWS Step Functions)
Designing event-driven, microservice, and/or multi-tier architectures based on requirements
Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements

stem: A SaaS platform emits domain events such as OrderCreated and SubscriptionCancelled. Multiple internal and partner applications need different subsets of these events. The producer team does not want to hardcode consumer endpoints or modify producer code whenever a new consumer is added. Which TWO design choices BEST meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Publish events to a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus.
answers.B: Create Amazon EventBridge rules with event patterns that route only relevant events to each target.
answers.C: Send all events to one Amazon SQS queue and require every consumer to poll the queue and discard events it does not need.
answers.D: Use AWS Step Functions as the central event router for all dynamic consumers.
answers.E: Push events directly from the producer to each consumer's HTTPS endpoint so the producer controls delivery.

explanation: Amazon EventBridge decouples producers from consumers and allows new targets to be added by defining additional rules rather than changing producer logic. Pattern-based routing lets each consumer receive only the events it needs, which is more loosely coupled and operationally cleaner than a shared queue or direct point-to-point delivery.
tags: Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements
Designing event-driven, microservice, and/or multi-tier architectures based on requirements

stem: A company exposes a REST API that accepts video-rendering requests from users. Rendering can take up to 20 minutes, request volume is bursty, and the API must return quickly with a job ID while workers scale independently of the API tier. Which architecture BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda to perform the rendering synchronously and return the final video URL when the function completes.
answers.B: Use Amazon API Gateway to submit jobs to an Amazon SQS queue, process them with Amazon ECS tasks on AWS Fargate, and store job status in Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.C: Place the API behind an Application Load Balancer and have the web tier call the rendering service synchronously on Amazon EC2 instances.
answers.D: Publish each request to Amazon SNS and ask users to retry until the notification email arrives.

explanation: A queue-based design decouples the API from the long-running rendering workers so the API can return immediately with a job identifier. Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate can handle render tasks longer than AWS Lambda time limits, and Amazon DynamoDB is a simple store for job state that supports bursty scale.
tags: Decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently
Serverless technologies and patterns (for example, AWS Lambda, Fargate)
Queuing and messaging concepts (for example, publish/subscribe)

stem: A company runs a multi-tier application in one AWS Region. Database changes must replicate to a second Region with an RPO of less than 5 minutes. In a disaster, the company must restore service in the second Region within 30 minutes at reduced but functional capacity. The company wants lower ongoing cost than an active-active design. Which disaster recovery strategy BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Backup and restore
answers.B: Pilot light
answers.C: Warm standby
answers.D: Multi-site active-active

explanation: Warm standby maintains a scaled-down but functional copy of the application stack in the recovery Region, which supports faster recovery than pilot light or backup and restore while costing less than active-active. The stated RPO and RTO fit a warm standby approach well.
tags: Disaster recovery (DR) strategies (for example, backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active failover, recovery point objective [RPO], recovery time objective [RTO])
Selecting an appropriate DR strategy to meet business requirements
AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A legacy web application on Amazon EC2 stores user-uploaded files on the local instance filesystem. The company needs the application to survive instance replacement and an Availability Zone failure with minimal code changes. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Move uploaded files to Amazon EFS mounted by all application instances.
answers.B: Place the instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer.
answers.C: Enable sticky sessions on the Application Load Balancer and keep file uploads on instance storage.
answers.D: Snapshot the instance store volumes every hour and restore them after a failure.
answers.E: Store uploads in the /tmp directory and rely on EC2 instance recovery.

explanation: Amazon EFS externalizes the file dependency with shared durable storage, and a multi-AZ Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer removes the dependency on any individual instance or Availability Zone. Sticky sessions and local storage preserve the original single-instance failure mode.
tags: Using AWS services that improve the reliability of legacy applications and applications not built for the cloud (for example, when application changes are not possible)
Implementing designs to mitigate single points of failure
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company connects its data center to AWS for a mission-critical application. Requirements are predictable bandwidth for steady traffic, encryption in transit, and automatic failover if the primary private connection fails. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use a single AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the VPC over the internet.
answers.B: Use AWS Direct Connect for the primary connection and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection as backup.
answers.C: Use VPC peering between the data center and the VPC and add Amazon CloudFront for failover.
answers.D: Use AWS PrivateLink from the data center to the VPC and add an internet gateway for fallback.

explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides predictable private bandwidth, and a Site-to-Site VPN can provide encrypted failover if the Direct Connect path is unavailable. The other options either do not provide the required private connectivity model or are not valid connectivity patterns for an on-premises data center.
tags: Network connection options (for example, AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink)
Selecting the appropriate bandwidth allocation for a network device (for example, a single VPN compared with multiple VPNs, Direct Connect speed)

stem: A company must deploy third-party virtual firewall appliances that inspect traffic between application VPCs and the internet. The solution needs transparent insertion, high availability, and the ability to scale the appliances without reconfiguring each workload VPC whenever capacity changes. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Place the appliances behind a Network Load Balancer and update routes in every VPC each time appliance capacity changes.
answers.B: Use a Gateway Load Balancer with the firewall appliances as targets and deploy Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the workload VPCs.
answers.C: Place the appliances behind an Application Load Balancer and use path-based routing to the inspection tier.
answers.D: Use Amazon CloudFront in front of the appliances so workloads can automatically fail over between firewall instances.

explanation: Gateway Load Balancer is designed for transparent insertion and scaling of third-party virtual appliances. Gateway Load Balancer endpoints simplify service insertion into workload VPCs without requiring constant route redesign as appliance capacity changes.
tags: Selecting the appropriate load balancing strategy
Creating a network topology for various architectures (for example, global, hybrid, multi-tier)
Determining network configurations that can scale to accommodate future needs

stem: A company has an on-premises SMB file share that employees actively use on site. Files older than 90 days are rarely accessed but must remain visible through the same share path. The company wants to move cold data to AWS at the lowest cost while retaining a local cache for hot files and minimizing changes to user workflows. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway on premises.
answers.B: Store the files in Amazon S3 and use lifecycle rules to transition older objects to Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes as appropriate.
answers.C: Replace the SMB share with Amazon EFS mounted over the internet from user desktops.
answers.D: Move all files to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in AWS and require every user to access it remotely over a dedicated connection at all times.
answers.E: Back up the file share to Amazon EBS snapshots each night and restore files on demand.

explanation: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway preserves the on-premises SMB experience while storing files in Amazon S3 and caching frequently used content locally. Amazon S3 lifecycle transitions can then move older files into lower-cost Amazon S3 Glacier classes without changing user access paths.
tags: Hybrid storage options (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Storage Gateway)
Storage tiering (for example, cold tiering for object storage)

stem: A company runs a stateless Java-based API on Amazon EC2. Profiling shows the workload is consistently CPU-bound, has no x86 dependency, and runs continuously at a stable baseline. The company wants to reduce compute cost without redesigning the application. Which change provides the BEST immediate cost optimization while preserving the workload's performance characteristics?

answers.A: Move the workload to memory-optimized x86 instances to reduce CPU contention.
answers.B: Move the workload to compute-optimized AWS Graviton-based instances after compatibility validation.
answers.C: Replace the Auto Scaling group with one large general purpose instance.
answers.D: Move the workload to AWS Lambda with provisioned concurrency sized to match the current EC2 fleet.

explanation: For a steady CPU-bound workload with no x86 dependency, compute-optimized AWS Graviton-based instances can lower cost while matching the performance profile more closely than general purpose or memory-optimized instances. The other choices either misalign with the workload profile or require a larger architectural change.
tags: Instance types, families, and sizes (for example, memory optimized, compute optimized, virtualization)
Selecting the appropriate instance family for a workload
Determining cost-effective AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate)

stem: A company runs non-production Amazon ECS tasks that process asynchronous jobs. The tasks are stateless, checkpoint progress externally, and can tolerate interruption. The team wants to minimize cost and avoid managing EC2 instances. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Run the tasks on Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2 On-Demand instances in an Auto Scaling group.
answers.B: Run the tasks on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate Spot capacity.
answers.C: Move the tasks to Amazon EKS with managed node groups on On-Demand instances.
answers.D: Run the tasks as synchronous AWS Lambda invocations behind an Application Load Balancer.

explanation: AWS Fargate Spot reduces cost for interruptible, stateless container tasks while preserving the no-server-management model. Because the tasks can tolerate interruption and checkpoint state externally, the Spot model aligns well with the workload characteristics.
tags: AWS purchasing options (for example, Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans)
Determining cost-effective AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate)
Optimization of compute utilization (for example, containers, serverless computing, microservices)

stem: An ecommerce application uses MySQL and is read-heavy during daytime catalog browsing. The primary database handles writes easily, but read traffic drives most of the cost. The company wants to keep MySQL compatibility and minimize cost while scaling reads independently of writes. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition with reader Auto Scaling and direct read traffic to the reader endpoint.
answers.B: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB on-demand and use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for writes.
answers.C: Use Amazon RDS for SQL Server Multi-AZ with one larger instance class.
answers.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache as the only persistent data store for product catalog records.

explanation: Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition preserves MySQL compatibility and can scale read capacity independently by adding reader instances, including with Auto Scaling. This directly addresses a read-heavy cost driver without forcing a major application rewrite or misuse of a cache as the system of record.
tags: Configuring read replicas to meet business requirements
Determining cost-effective AWS database services with appropriate use cases (for example, DynamoDB compared with Amazon RDS, serverless)

stem: A company runs ad hoc analytical SQL queries on several terabytes of historical operational data a few times each month. The workload is not continuous, concurrency is low, and the company wants to avoid managing infrastructure or paying for idle clusters. Which database solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Amazon Aurora provisioned cluster
answers.B: Amazon Redshift Serverless
answers.C: Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ
answers.D: Amazon DynamoDB on-demand

explanation: Amazon Redshift Serverless is designed for analytics workloads that need SQL over large historical datasets without always-on cluster management. It is more cost-effective for infrequent ad hoc analytical use than provisioned relational databases that would sit idle between query bursts.
tags: Determining cost-effective AWS database types (for example, time series format, columnar format)
Determining cost-effective AWS database services with appropriate use cases (for example, DynamoDB compared with Amazon RDS, serverless)

stem: A company serves large static product images from an Amazon S3 bucket to users around the world. The images are the main source of internet data transfer cost and user latency. The company wants to reduce both origin transfer cost and end-user latency with minimal application changes. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

answers.A: Place Amazon CloudFront in front of the Amazon S3 bucket and cache the images at edge locations.
answers.B: Use AWS Global Accelerator with the Amazon S3 bucket as the endpoint.
answers.C: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for every object request and keep direct S3 URLs in the application.
answers.D: Route image requests through a NAT gateway in the nearest AWS Region to each user.

explanation: Amazon CloudFront reduces latency by caching content close to users and can also reduce origin data transfer from Amazon S3 by serving repeated requests from the edge. This matches both the performance and cost goals with minimal changes to the application architecture.
tags: Determining strategic needs for content delivery networks (CDNs) and edge caching
Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations

stem: An ad-tech company serves fraud-risk predictions from a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Traffic is usually steady at 40 requests/second, but product launches create predictable 10-minute spikes to 400 requests/second. The team must keep p95 latency under 120 ms during launches while minimizing idle cost outside spikes. Which endpoint scaling configuration best meets these requirements?
tags: How to use SageMaker endpoint auto scaling policies to meet scalability requirements (e.g., based on demand, time)
Choosing specific metrics for auto scaling (e.g., model latency, CPU utilization, invocations per instance)

answers.A: Use target tracking on InvocationsPerInstance and add scheduled scaling to raise desired capacity before launch windows, with a lower minimum capacity after events.
answers.B: Use step scaling only on CPUUtilization and keep min capacity at one instance to maximize savings when traffic is low.
answers.C: Use target tracking on model latency alone and remove cooldown periods so scale-out can trigger repeatedly every minute.
answers.D: Disable auto scaling and run one larger instance type that can absorb peak load without changing instance count.

explanation: A is correct because predictable launch windows are best handled by scheduled pre-scaling, while target tracking on invocations per instance handles intra-window variation without permanently overprovisioning. B is wrong because CPU does not reliably represent inference queue pressure and min=1 is risky for sharp predictable bursts. C is wrong because latency-only tracking can react too late during sudden ramp-ups, and removing cooldowns often causes oscillation. D is wrong because fixed peak-sized capacity wastes cost for most hours and does not adapt to growth pattern changes.

stem: A platform team maintains a foundation stack with VPC subnets, security groups, and a KMS key. An ML team must deploy SageMaker models into those shared resources across dev, stage, and prod with minimal manual edits and repeatable promotions. Which IaC approach provides the most maintainable cross-stack provisioning pattern?
tags: Tradeoffs and use cases of infrastructure as code (IaC) options (e.g., AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit [AWS CDK])
Automating the provisioning of compute resources, including communication between stacks (e.g., by using CloudFormation, AWS CDK)
Deploying and hosting models by using the SageMaker SDK

answers.A: Keep separate templates per environment and hardcode subnet IDs and key ARNs for each deployment stage.
answers.B: Publish shared resource outputs from the foundation stack and consume them as typed inputs in a CDK or CloudFormation model-deployment stack promoted through one pipeline.
answers.C: Run a pre-deploy script that queries resource IDs with AWS CLI and injects them as ad hoc parameter overrides at release time.
answers.D: Place network, security, and model resources in one large template and redeploy the whole stack for every model version update.

explanation: B is correct because explicit stack outputs and typed imports create stable contracts between teams, reduce drift, and support repeatable promotions across environments. A is wrong because hardcoded IDs create brittle templates and high maintenance overhead. C is wrong because ad hoc CLI discovery is error-prone and undermines reproducibility in CI/CD. D is wrong because a monolithic template couples unrelated lifecycle changes and increases deployment blast radius.

stem: A retailer has a custom inference stack with nonstandard native libraries. The model must run on SageMaker in private subnets, and security requires immutable container artifacts plus controlled image provenance for audits. Which deployment pattern best satisfies these requirements?
tags: Containerization concepts and AWS container services
Building and maintaining containers (e.g., Amazon Elastic Container Registry [Amazon ECR], Amazon EKS, Amazon ECS, by using bring your own container [BYOC] with SageMaker)
Configuring SageMaker endpoints within the VPC network

answers.A: Build the container on a developer laptop, push it to a public registry, and reference that image URI from a SageMaker model.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker prebuilt image and install missing native dependencies during container startup for each endpoint instance.
answers.C: Build a BYOC image in CI, scan and sign it, store it in Amazon ECR, and deploy the endpoint in private subnets with tightly scoped security groups.
answers.D: Package the inference service for Amazon ECS on Fargate and call it from SageMaker through a custom Lambda proxy layer.

explanation: C is correct because a CI-built BYOC image in ECR supports immutable, auditable artifacts and is the standard approach for custom runtime dependencies on SageMaker. A is wrong due to weak provenance and public-registry governance risk. B is wrong because runtime package installation breaks immutability and creates inconsistent startup behavior. D is wrong because it adds an unnecessary multi-service indirection when SageMaker can directly host the custom container.

stem: A logistics company runs route-optimization inference on a SageMaker endpoint. Demand is low most of the day, but every weekday from 06:30 to 08:30 traffic becomes sustained and latency-sensitive as dispatch planning starts. The team wants predictable performance during the window and lower spend outside it. Which resource strategy is most appropriate?
tags: Difference between on-demand and provisioned resources

Applying best practices to enable maintainable, scalable, and cost-effective ML solutions (e.g., automatic scaling on SageMaker endpoints, dynamically adding Spot Instances, by using Amazon EC2 Instances, by using Lambda behind the endpoints)

answers.A: Use target tracking only with a very low minimum capacity and allow scaling to react after the morning surge has already started.
answers.B: Use scheduled scaling to pre-warm capacity before 06:30 and combine it with target tracking during the window, then scale down after 08:30.
answers.C: Keep a fixed provisioned fleet sized for the morning peak all day to avoid any scaling decisions during business hours.
answers.D: Move to a serverless endpoint with no schedule and rely solely on cold-start behavior to absorb the predictable weekday spike.

explanation: B is correct because predictable peaks should be handled with scheduled pre-scaling, while target tracking covers day-to-day variance and allows aggressive scale-down after the window. A is wrong because reactive scaling alone may violate latency at surge start. C is wrong because peak-sized all-day capacity is cost-inefficient. D is wrong because relying only on serverless cold starts for a known sustained latency-sensitive window is a weaker fit for predictable performance.

stem: A genomics company runs bursty HPC pipelines on Amazon EC2. Each run needs a shared POSIX file system that can deliver very high throughput to thousands of Linux workers, and the input data already resides in an Amazon S3 data lake. The company wants the scratch file system to scale out for the job and avoid keeping duplicate permanent copies of the data. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Create an Amazon EFS file system in General Purpose mode, mount it on all workers, and copy the S3 dataset into the file system before each run.
answers.B: Deploy Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket, mount it on the workers during each run, and use the file system as the shared scratch layer.
answers.C: Provision a large gp3 Amazon EBS volume, attach it to one EC2 instance, and export it to the workers by using NFS from that instance.
answers.D: Store the scratch files directly in Amazon S3 and mount the bucket on each worker by using an S3 file system driver.

explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is correct because it provides high-throughput, shared POSIX storage for HPC workloads and can link to an existing S3 bucket so the workers can process S3-backed datasets without creating a separate permanent copy. Amazon EFS is elastic and shared, but it is not the best fit for this kind of massively parallel scratch workload. A single gp3 volume exported from one EC2 instance creates a bottleneck and single point of failure. Mounting Amazon S3 through a file system driver does not provide the same POSIX semantics or performance profile that the HPC job requires.
tags: Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs
Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)

stem: A media company keeps 120 TB of active project files in an on-premises NAS. Editors in six branch offices need local-LAN read performance for recently used files, but all offices must work from one centralized copy in AWS and the company does not want to rewrite client workflows that already use SMB shares. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.A: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway in each branch office, expose SMB shares to the editors, and store the files centrally in Amazon S3 with each gateway using its local cache.
answers.B: Create an Amazon EFS file system in one Region, connect every branch office to the file system over Site-to-Site VPN, and migrate the NAS data directly into EFS.
answers.C: Deploy Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in AWS, map the share across all offices, and disable local caching so every read is served from the Region.
answers.D: Replicate the NAS data to a separate Amazon S3 bucket for each branch office and use S3 bucket policies so the editors can choose the closest bucket.

explanation: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway is correct because it presents standard SMB shares to each office, keeps frequently accessed files in a local cache for low-latency reads, and stores the authoritative data set centrally in Amazon S3. Amazon EFS would require every file operation to traverse the WAN and would not preserve the same branch-local caching model. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server can provide SMB storage, but without a local gateway cache each office would still depend on Regional network latency for every read. Replicating separate S3 buckets per office increases complexity and does not preserve the existing SMB-based workflow for the editors.
tags: Hybrid storage solutions to meet business requirements
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs
Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)

stem: A company is moving a latency-sensitive transactional database to Amazon EC2. The database will keep all data on a single block device and requires 18,000 sustained IOPS at sub-millisecond latency during business hours. The workload must preserve that performance even when the volume size remains relatively small. Which storage option is the best fit?

answers.A: Use a gp3 Amazon EBS volume and provision 16,000 IOPS with 1,000 MiB/s of throughput.
answers.B: Use a throughput optimized HDD (st1) Amazon EBS volume sized large enough to increase baseline throughput.
answers.C: Use an io2 Amazon EBS volume sized for the database and provision the required IOPS for consistent low-latency performance.
answers.D: Use an Amazon EFS file system with Provisioned Throughput mode and mount it to the database instance.

explanation: An io2 Amazon EBS volume is correct because it is designed for databases that need sustained, low-latency IOPS independent of large capacity allocation. A gp3 volume is cost-effective for many workloads, but it tops out below the required 18,000 IOPS in this scenario. An st1 volume is optimized for throughput, not for high random IOPS at low latency. Amazon EFS is shared file storage, not a block device designed for a single-instance transactional database that needs predictable IOPS.
tags: Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Storage types with associated characteristics (for example, object, file, block)
Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)

stem: A retailer runs nightly ETL jobs on Amazon EC2 instances. Each job writes sequentially to a single Amazon EBS volume and needs about 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s of throughput for four hours every night. The team wants the least expensive block storage option that can be tuned to these requirements without overprovisioning capacity. Which solution should the team choose?

answers.A: Use an io2 Amazon EBS volume with enough provisioned IOPS to cover the job window.
answers.B: Use a gp2 Amazon EBS volume and increase the size until the baseline performance reaches the target.
answers.C: Use a cold HDD (sc1) Amazon EBS volume and rely on burst credits during the ETL window.
answers.D: Use a gp3 Amazon EBS volume and provision the required IOPS and throughput independently from capacity.

explanation: A gp3 Amazon EBS volume is correct because gp3 allows the team to set IOPS and throughput separately from volume size, which is ideal when the performance requirement is known but the team wants to avoid paying for unnecessary capacity. An io2 volume would meet the requirement but at a higher cost than necessary for this sequential ETL workload. A gp2 volume would require the team to buy more capacity just to raise baseline performance. An sc1 volume is intended for cold, infrequently accessed data and is not appropriate for this level of nightly ETL performance.
tags: Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs
Storage types with associated characteristics (for example, object, file, block)

stem: A financial services company runs Apache Spark jobs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Each job rebuilds its intermediate shuffle data from source records in Amazon S3 if a node fails. The workload needs the highest possible local read and write performance for the temporary files, and the company wants to avoid paying for persistent storage that is discarded after every run. Which design should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.A: Store the shuffle data on Amazon EFS so every node can access one shared file system.
answers.B: Choose EC2 instances with local instance store volumes and write the temporary shuffle data to the instance store.
answers.C: Attach gp3 Amazon EBS volumes to every node and snapshot the volumes after each processing stage.
answers.D: Write the shuffle data back to Amazon S3 and use byte-range GET requests when later stages need it.

explanation: EC2 instance store is correct because the shuffle files are temporary, can be recreated from Amazon S3, and need very high local I/O performance without paying for persistent storage after the job ends. Amazon EFS provides shared file storage, but it adds network hops and is not the best fit for ephemeral high-speed scratch data. Gp3 volumes are persistent and would add cost for data the workload intentionally discards. Writing the intermediate data back to Amazon S3 would reduce performance because the shuffle workload needs low-latency local storage, not durable object storage.

stem: A software company runs containerized rendering jobs across multiple Availability Zones. The jobs must share one POSIX-compliant file system for common assets, and throughput spikes unpredictably during release days. The company must guarantee at least 300 MiB/s of file system throughput without sizing the file system far beyond its current 4 TiB footprint. Which solution best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use an Amazon EFS Regional file system and configure Provisioned Throughput for the required baseline throughput.
answers.B: Use an Amazon EFS One Zone file system in Bursting Throughput mode and depend on burst credits during release days.
answers.C: Use one large gp3 Amazon EBS volume, attach it to a single EC2 instance, and re-export the file system to the containers over NFS.
answers.D: Use Amazon S3 with an object-mounted file system so every container can read the shared assets directly.

explanation: Amazon EFS with Provisioned Throughput is correct because it gives the company a shared Regional file system across multiple Availability Zones and guarantees the required throughput without forcing the team to overprovision file system size. An EFS One Zone file system would not provide the same multi-AZ resilience, and Bursting mode would not guarantee the required baseline. Re-exporting a single gp3 volume through one EC2 instance creates both a bottleneck and a single point of failure. Mounting Amazon S3 as if it were a file system does not provide the POSIX semantics and throughput behavior that the rendering jobs require.

explanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is correct because it supports both NFS and SMB access to the same underlying data and provides enterprise file system features such as snapshots and writable clones. Amazon EFS is primarily NFS-based and does not satisfy the Windows SMB requirement. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is strong for SMB workloads, but it does not provide the same multiprotocol model for shared Linux and Windows access to the same datasets. Amazon S3 is object storage and is not the right replacement for a shared enterprise file system with these protocol and cloning requirements.
